text: eVitals RPM Platform — Comprehensive Knowledge Base (RAG-Optimized)

This document is a comprehensive, retrieval-optimized knowledge base describing the eVitals Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM) platform. It was derived entirely from the eVitals User Guide, Version 2.4 (“the source manual”), the single source of truth for this document. Every factual claim below — every role privilege, field, workflow, CPT code, device rule, and business rule — is grounded in the source manual’s text, tables, numbered steps, and screenshots. Where the source manual did not specify something (a clinical threshold, a numeric limit, a downstream system behavior), this document says so explicitly rather than inventing an answer.
This document is written for consumption by a Retrieval-Augmented-Generation (RAG) system answering natural-language questions about eVitals. Each section is self-contained: it repeats the module name, screen name, and navigation path rather than referring back to “the section above,” so that a single retrieved chunk carries enough context to answer a question on its own.
How to read “Not specified in the user guide.” Wherever this exact phrase appears, it means the source manual does not state an answer to that specific question, and no answer should be inferred from general RPM/CCM industry knowledge, medical billing conventions, or assumptions about how similar platforms typically behave.

eVitals is a Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM) platform. It gives practices a single workspace to enroll patients, capture vitals from connected devices, run scheduled follow-ups, and produce billing-ready evidence of service time.
What problem eVitals solves. Practices that bill Medicare/insurance for RPM and CCM services must be able to prove, per patient and per billing cycle, that qualifying devices were supplied, that a minimum number of measurement days occurred, and that a minimum amount of clinical/caregiver service time was spent reviewing the patient’s data. eVitals centralizes patient enrollment, device/serial-number assignment, vitals capture, caregiver follow-up documentation, scheduling, secure messaging, and the billing/CPT-eligibility reporting that turns all of that activity into submittable billing evidence.
Who uses eVitals. Seven system roles are defined on the platform:
Super Admin — the platform-wide operator. Provisions practices, organization-level Admins, and platform-wide programs. Has no practice-count restriction; can see and manage every practice on the platform.
Admin (also referred to in the source manual as “System Admin”) — a cross-practice operator for a customer organization. Works inside the specific set of practices assigned to them and holds nearly the same day-to-day management rights as the Super Admin, minus platform-level provisioning (practice enrollment, Email Logs, and Mobile App Access are Super-Admin-only).
Practice Admin — manages a single practice: its clinicians (Providers), its practice-employed Caregivers, and its patients. Bound to exactly one practice; cannot switch to or view any other practice.
Provider — the clinician (physician / NP) who reviews vitals, enrolls and edits patients, manages the practice’s calendar, and signs off on billing. Sees practice-administration tabs (Practice, Admins, other Providers) for reference only — those tabs are read-only for a Provider.
Practice Caregiver — a practice-employed caregiver who runs day-to-day monitoring and follow-up for the patients of a single practice. Has no access to Admins/Providers/Inventory/Billing/Calendar/Programs/Permission modules.
System Caregiver — an eVitals-employed caregiver shared across multiple practices, assigned by a Super Admin or Admin. A read-and-monitor role: assigned-practices list, patient lookups, follow-up queries, messages, and account settings only. Cannot add, edit, or delete patient or practice records.
Patient — the end user of the mobile companion app (out of scope for this volume of the guide, which documents the web portal roles above).
Core objects and how they relate. A Practice is the top-level tenant that a Super Admin provisions. A practice has Practice Admins, Providers, and Practice Caregivers (practice-employed) plus optionally-assigned System Caregivers (shared, eVitals-employed). A practice enrolls Patients into one or both Care Programs — Chronic Care Management (CCM) and Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM). An RPM-enrolled patient is bound to one or more physical devices (blood-pressure monitor, glucometer, weight scale), each identified by a Model Number and a Serial Number, drawn from the practice’s or platform’s Inventory. Devices transmit vital readings (Blood Pressure/Pulse, Blood Glucose, Weight/Body Fat) which are evaluated against the practice’s configured Schedule & Targets (reading windows and normal ranges). Accumulated Measurement Days and caregiver/provider Service Time are evaluated against CPT code eligibility rules and rolled up into the Billing module for each program’s billing cycle. Care Management (Follow Up Query) surfaces patients who need caregiver outreach because of missed uploads, abnormal readings, or pending care-plan items; caregivers document outreach using reusable Follow Up templates configured under Settings. Calendar lets practice staff (Practice Admin, Provider) define bookable Visit Types and Working Hours and schedule appointments, with Calendar Permission controlling which System Caregivers may create/view/edit/delete on that calendar. Messages is the platform’s internal HIPAA-secured chat, gated per pairing by Chat Access settings. Permission (Role-Based Access Control) defines what each of the seven built-in roles — and any custom roles a Super Admin creates — is allowed to view, add, edit, or delete.
Document structure note. The source manual is written as a Hierarchical Task Analysis (HTA): every feature is decomposed into Module → Sub-module/Screen → Task → Steps → UI Reference, and nearly every module is documented once per role, because each role sees a different subset of fields, tabs, and permitted actions on what is otherwise the same screen. This knowledge base follows the source’s module boundaries and exact terminology, but consolidates the six operator-role chapters (Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, System Caregiver) into unified module sections, calling out role-specific differences explicitly wherever the source manual documents a difference in view/add/edit/delete rights, visible fields, or scope. This avoids repeating near-identical procedural text six times while preserving every documented role distinction.

RPM (Remote Patient Monitoring). The care program built around connected devices (BP monitor, glucometer, scale) that transmit vital readings from the patient’s home. Billed under CPT codes 99453, 99454, 99457, 99458 (see Section 13 — Billing and CPT Codes).
CCM (Chronic Care Management). The care program for patients with two or more qualifying chronic conditions who receive ongoing non-face-to-face care coordination. Billed under CPT codes 99490, 99439, and 99491.
CPT Code. Current Procedural Terminology billing code. eVitals computes “Eligible CPT Codes” per patient per billing cycle from recorded Measurement Days and Service Time; see Section 13.
Measurement Days. The count of unique calendar days within a billing window on which the patient uploaded at least one qualifying vital reading. Drives RPM device-supply billing (CPT 99454).
Service Time. Minutes of caregiver or provider review/interaction time accrued in the current billing cycle. Drives RPM treatment-management billing (CPT 99457/99458) and CCM care-coordination billing (CPT 99490/99439/99491).
Billing Cycle. The date-bounded window (Start Date + configured cycle length in days = End Date) against which a practice’s RPM or CCM billing is evaluated. Configured per practice, per program, under Enrollment / Care Program Billing Cycles.
Chronic Conditions. ICD-coded diagnoses that qualify a patient for CCM enrollment; the source manual states CCM billing under CPT 99490 requires two or more chronic conditions to be selected on the patient’s CCM enrollment step.
Model Number. The manufacturer’s model identifier for a device/meter (e.g., a specific BP-cuff or glucometer model), tracked at the Inventory product level and again on each patient’s device mapping.
Serial Number. The unique identifier of one physical device unit. On the patient-enrollment “Meter Mapping” step, the Meter Serial Number field requires exactly 16 characters; Save/Next remains disabled until the length matches. A serial number already bound to another patient is rejected.
Gateway Serial Number. An optional serial number for a cellular hub/gateway device, captured at Inventory add/edit time and, optionally, at patient meter-mapping time.
Vitals. The measured values captured by RPM devices: Blood Pressure (Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse), Blood Glucose (mg/dL), and Weight (lb, plus derived Body Fat % and BMI).
Reading Window. A configured time-of-day band (e.g., “Morning 06:00–15:59”) within which a reading of a given vital type is expected/classified; configured per practice under Schedule & Targets.
Target Range. The configured lower/upper bound for a vital within a given reading window; readings outside the range are flagged as abnormal/out-of-range on the Patients grid.
BMI Reference Bands. Fixed, non-editable clinical reference values shown alongside the (editable) Weight Target Range: Underweight (BMI < 18.5), Normal Weight (18.5–24.9), Overweight (25.0–29.9), Obese (≥ 30.0).
Status (Practice/User). Active or Inactive. An Inactive practice status blocks new device orders, uploads, and billing until reactivated.
Status (Patient). Active / Paused (also shown as “Pending” in some grids) / Lost (also shown as “Left” or “L” in status chips), depending on the screen.
A / P / L chips. Summary-card and grid badges meaning Active / Pending / Locked (on Billing screens) or Active / Pending / Left (on Patient summary cards) — the exact meaning is screen-dependent; see the specific module section.
T / A / P / L badges (Billing). On the Billing Management practice list, four colored chips under “Patients Status”: T = Total patients in the billing period; A = Active (meeting service-time thresholds); P = Pending (partial data / awaiting review); L = Locked (billing already finalized for the cycle).
Eligible CPT Codes. A live, system-calculated column shown on billing/lookup reports listing every CPT code the patient currently qualifies for in the selected billing window, based on recorded Measurement Days, Service Time, and (for CCM) Complexity/Billing Path.
Complexity (CCM). Non-Complex / Complex, reflecting the patient’s care-plan configuration for the cycle; shown on the CCM billing report but not manually entered on that screen — it is computed from the underlying care plan.
Billing Path (CCM). A CCM billing-report column reflecting how the patient’s CCM service is being billed for the cycle (e.g., caregiver-provided vs. physician-provided care coordination), likewise derived from the care plan rather than typed in on the report screen. The full set of Billing Path values is not specified in the user guide.
Buying Device. A practice-level Monitoring Details flag: Yes means the practice purchases RPM devices outright; No means eVitals leases devices for the program.
Two-Way / Two Factor Authentication (2FA). An account-level toggle requiring an emailed one-time password (OTP) at every sign-in.
Event Logs. An audit-trail control (button/link) present at the bottom of most role/practice-user grids (Admins, Providers, Caregivers, System Caregivers, Inventory, Billing, Schedule & Targets, etc.) that opens a chronological history of add/edit/delete/assignment actions for that grid.
Email Logs. The platform-wide (Super Admin / Admin) audit trail of every outbound system email — OTPs, password resets, alerts — independent of the per-module Event Logs.
Focused Vital Snapshot. A panel inside the Messages screen that, when a patient is searched by name or ID, displays that patient’s latest vitals alongside the chat thread.
Follow Up Template. A reusable note template (configured under Settings → Follow Up) that pre-fills structured fields — Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate, a symptom/adherence checklist, recommended actions, and (for CCM) a “care management contact completed” line and Conditions Addressed / Activity fields — for caregivers documenting a patient follow-up.
Chat Access. A Settings-module control (practice-scoped) that allows or blocks messaging between specific Caregiver↔Patient, Provider↔Patient, or Caregiver↔Provider pairs.
Calendar Permission. A Settings-module control that grants a named System Caregiver any combination of Create / View / Edit / Delete rights on a practice’s or Provider’s calendar.
Permission (RBAC). The Role-Based Access Control surface (Super Admin / Admin only) listing all built-in and custom roles with a per-module View/Add/Edit/Delete permission matrix.
Mobile App Access. A per-user, per-practice toggle (Super Admin, under Settings) controlling whether a user account may sign in to the eVitals mobile companion app; independent of web-portal access.
MRN. Medical Record Number; the field the bulk-patient Import process treats as the idempotency key (a duplicate MRN row is skipped rather than creating a duplicate patient). The exact source/format of the MRN field on the enrollment wizard itself is not specified in the user guide.
NPI. National Provider Identifier; a field captured when adding a Provider.
ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes. Diagnosis codes selectable when configuring a Care Program’s Clinical Requirements (qualifying diagnoses) and when documenting a patient’s Chronic Conditions for CCM.
Hierarchical Task Analysis (HTA). The documentation methodology used by the source manual itself: Module → Sub-module → Task → Steps → UI Reference, with a colored meta-box per task carrying Goal / Actor / Access Path / Preconditions / Outcome.

Every eVitals user is assigned exactly one role (custom roles can also be created by a Super Admin under Settings → Permission). The seven built-in roles are: Super Admin (Role Id 1), Admin (2), Practice Admin (3), Provider (4), Practice CareGiver (5), Patient (6), System Caregiver (7). A ninth built-in identifier, “superadminrole” (Role Id 9), also appears in the Permission role list. Built-in roles cannot be deleted; only custom roles can be removed. The Super Admin role (Role Id 1) exposes only an Edit icon in the Permission table — users cannot be assigned to it through the Assign User interface shown for other roles.
Role determines: which sidebar modules are visible, which tabs within the Practice/Dashboard workspace are visible, and — per module — whether View/Add/Edit/Delete actions are exposed. The tables below reproduce each role’s “privileges at a glance” summary as documented in the source manual, followed by a narrative capability description and explicit role-vs-role differences.

Sees every practice on the platform with no scope restriction.

Purpose. Establish an authenticated session against a user’s role. This is the entry point for every eVitals role — Authentication decides which dashboard and which module privileges the session receives.
Actor. All roles.
Access Path / Navigation. https://<tenant>.evitalsrpm.com/ — a public login page, no prior session required.
Preconditions. The user has an active account and a valid password.
Outcome. The user lands on their role’s default dashboard (Super Admin → Practice List; Admin → Dashboard with scoped Enrollment Summary; Practice Admin/Provider → assigned practice; Practice Caregiver → assigned practice patient roster; System Caregiver → Practices List).
Procedure: 1. Open the eVitals login URL. 2. Enter the registered Email address (case-insensitive) in the Email field. 3. Enter the Password in the Password field (a visibility toggle is available). 4. Optionally tick Remember me to keep the email pre-filled on this device (see 4.3 — this persists only the email, not the password). 5. Click Sign In. 6. If two-factor authentication (2FA) is enabled on the account, enter the OTP delivered by email and click Verify.
UI Reference — Login Window:
Field / Control | Description
Email | Registered email address (case-insensitive).
Password | Account password; visibility toggle available.
Remember me | Persists the email (not the password) in browser storage.
Forgot Password? | Opens the recovery flow (see 4.2).
Sign In | Submits credentials.
Privileges. View: Yes (all roles reach the login window at the tenant URL). Add: Not applicable (accounts are created by Super Admin/Admin/Practice Admin, not from this screen). Edit: No (no editable records on this screen). Delete: No. Sign in: Yes (email + password, then role-based redirect to the matching dashboard).

Purpose. Reset the account password when the user cannot sign in.
Actor. All roles.
Access Path. Login page → Forgot Password?
Preconditions. The user still controls the email address on file.
Outcome. A new password is set and the user can sign in.
Procedure: 1. Click Forgot Password? on the login page. 2. Enter the account email and submit. 3. Open the “E-Vitals Password Reset Request” email (this transactional email is auditable via Email Logs — see Section 17.6). 4. Follow the reset link and enter a new password meeting the strength criteria (length, case, digit, symbol rules — the exact numeric thresholds are not specified in the user guide beyond “shown live under the password field” during practice enrollment). 5. Return to the login page and sign in with the new password.
Privileges. View: Yes (reachable from the login window for all roles). Add: Not applicable. Edit: Yes (the user sets a new password from the emailed reset link). Delete: No. Send reset email: Yes (submitting the registered email triggers the reset mail).

The “Remember me” checkbox on the Login Window persists the entered email address (not the password) in browser storage on that device, so it is pre-filled on the next visit. The source manual documents this as a standalone task/module of the Authentication area alongside Login Window and Forget Password, with the same “all roles” actor scope. Beyond the description already given in Section 4.1, the source manual does not add further detail specific to this control (e.g., an explicit expiry period is not specified in the user guide).
Every role lands on a different default screen after login, reflecting its scope (platform-wide, cross-practice, single-practice, or read-only-cross-practice).

Purpose. Understand platform-wide reach at a glance and reach any Super Admin capability in one click.
Actor / Access Path. Super Admin; default landing view after sign-in.
What’s on screen — Enrollment Summary. Three summary cards at the top of the workspace:
Field / Control | Description
Total Practices | Number of practices provisioned on the platform.
Total Patients | Aggregate patient count across all practices.
Total Programs | Count of care programs configured (typically CCM & RPM).
Procedure — review summary and navigate: 1. Sign in as Super Admin. 2. Read the three summary cards at the top of the workspace. 3. Use the numbers as an entry point into deeper modules (e.g., click a practice row to drill in). 4. The persistent left sidebar is pinned to the left of every Super Admin screen; click a module (e.g., Patient Mgmt) to reveal its sub-items, then click the sub-item to load the workspace in the main pane. 5. Watch for red dots on sidebar icons — a red dot marks a module with items waiting for attention (e.g., Patient Mgmt, Care Mgmt).
Modules reachable from the Super Admin sidebar: Enrollment, Admins (System Admins), Caregivers (System Caregivers), Inventory, Billing, Patient Mgmt, Care Mgmt, Calendar, Programs, Settings (Settings itself, Permission, Email Logs, Mobile App), Messages.

Purpose. Get a portfolio-wide snapshot of practices, patients, and programs the Admin (System Admin) oversees, scoped to their assigned practices only.
Actor / Access Path. Admin (System Admin); Sidebar → Dashboard.
Preconditions. Signed in as an Admin.
Outcome. Three headline cards are visible: Total Practices, Total Patients, Total Programs, each showing role-scoped counts with A / P / L sub-badges (Active / Pending / Locked).
Procedure: 1. Sign in and land on the Dashboard by default. 2. Read the three summary cards: Total Practices, Total Patients, Total Programs. 3. Confirm the sub-badge counts (A#, P#, L#) match the practices this Admin manages. 4. Scroll to the Practice List table for drill-in.
Filter and open a practice: 1. Use the “Search practices…” box, or the Status, Locations, Patient Range, or Programs dropdowns to narrow the list. 2. Sort by clicking any column header (Status, Practice, Total Patients, Program Enrolled). 3. Click the blue eye (view) icon in the Action column on a practice row. 4. The practice detail view opens on the Practice tab, breadcrumb Dashboard > .
Note. Admin sees only practices they are assigned to, unlike Super Admin who sees all.

Purpose. Open the practice dashboard scoped to the Practice Admin’s single assigned practice.
Actor / Access Path. Practice Admin; Login → Dashboard.
Preconditions. Practice Admin credentials issued by Super Admin / Admin.
Outcome. The dashboard opens directly to the assigned practice (e.g., “Amir Mobile Test Practices”), showing CCM/RPM enrollment chips and the tab strip: Practice, Admins, Providers, Caregivers, Patients, System Caregivers, RPM, Schedule & Targets, Import Patients.
Procedure: 1. Sign in with Practice Admin credentials at the login page. 2. A green welcome toast (“Welcome back, practice admin!”) confirms the role. 3. The practice name and enrollment chips (e.g., 12 CCM, 30 RPM) appear at the top of the page. 4. Use the tab strip to switch between Practice, Admins, Providers, Caregivers, Patients, System Caregivers, RPM, Schedule & Targets, and Import Patients. 5. Use the left sidebar (Dashboard, Patient Mgmt, Care Mgmt, Calendar, Messages, Settings) to leave the practice-landing view.
Notes. A Practice Admin sees exactly one practice — the practice they were provisioned against — so there is no Practice List to pick from. A red dot on sidebar icons signals unread alerts for that module.

Purpose. Land the Provider on their assigned practice, confirm sign-in role, and expose the practice-detail tab bar.
Actor / Access Path. Provider; Login → Dashboard (auto-opens the Provider’s assigned practice).
Preconditions. The Provider is an active user attached to at least one practice.
Outcome. The practice name (e.g., “Amir Mobile Test Practices”) is displayed as the H1, the 12 CCM / 30 RPM enrollment counters are shown below the title, the Practice tab is preselected, and a toast confirms “Welcome back, <first name>! Signed in as Provider. You have successfully logged in to E-Vitals.”
Procedure: 1. Sign in with Provider credentials; the Dashboard opens on the assigned practice. 2. Read the welcome toast (top-right) to confirm role and practice. 3. Confirm the enrollment counters — <N> CCM (green heart) and <N> RPM (blue heart) — beneath the practice name. 4. Use the horizontal tab bar to move between Practice, Admins, Providers, Caregivers, Patients, System Caregivers, RPM, Schedule & Targets, Import Patients. 5. Use header shortcuts: the bell for notifications, the info (i) icon for release notes, and the username dropdown (top-right) for Logout / Change Password / My Account.
Notes. Providers see practice-scoped data only — the top-level Practice List / Enrollment views used by Super Admin and Admin are hidden. CCM/RPM counters on the header reflect currently enrolled patients across all statuses; use the Patients tab for a live filterable grid. The welcome toast can be dismissed with the × icon and will not reappear until the next login.

Purpose. Land on the assigned practice and review the patient panel with CCM/RPM enrollment counts and pending billing.
Actor. Practice Caregiver.
Precondition. The caregiver is signed in and assigned to at least one practice.
Outcome. A filtered patient list is visible with vitals, service time, and billing status per patient.
What’s on screen: - The practice header (e.g., “Amir Mobile Test Practices”) with CCM/RPM enrollment counts under the title, and a BILLING DATES block (top-right) showing the current RPM window (e.g., 07-27-2026 – 08-26-2026). - A KPI strip: Total Patients, Active Care Plan (provider-approved), Complex Care Plan (attested complex CCM), Items Pending Review (care-plan changes awaiting provider), and CPT Billing (99490 / 99491 / 99439 counters, or 99453/99445/99454 with a “+3 more” link depending on program view). - A Search patients by name… box and an All Status filter; CCM / RPM buttons to switch program context; + Add Patient to launch the enrollment wizard. - Per-row eye icon (open patient chart), pencil icon (edit patient); rows also surface DOB, chronic conditions, last activity, service time, and billing state (e.g., Pending).
Procedure: 1. Sign in as a Practice Caregiver — the workspace lands on the practice header with CCM/RPM enrollment counts under the title. 2. Read the KPI strip. 3. Use the Search box or All Status filter to narrow the list; click CCM or RPM to switch program context; or click + Add Patient to launch the enrollment wizard. 4. For any row, click the eye icon to open the patient chart, or the pencil icon to edit that patient.
Notes. Status chips read A = Active, P = Pending, L = Left/inactive. Service Time (Min) accumulates toward CPT time thresholds; Readings feeds the (16-day) requirement referenced for CPT 99454. N/A in a vitals column means no reading has been received for that vital in the current window.

The System Caregiver has no platform-wide dashboard of its own. Signing in lands the role on the Practices List — the set of practices the caregiver is assigned to — which acts as the role’s home screen.
Purpose. Review the practices the System Caregiver is assigned to and drill into a practice for context.
Actor. System Caregiver.
Precondition. A Super Admin/Admin has assigned the caregiver to at least one practice.
Outcome. The caregiver can open a practice card and proceed to patient-scoped work under that practice.
What’s on screen. A Practices List with columns #, Practice Name, Email, Phone 1, Phone 2, Address, Fax, and Action.
Procedure: 1. Sign in as a System Caregiver — the workspace lands on the Practices List. 2. Use the All Programs dropdown (top-right) to filter practices by enrolled program (e.g., CCM, RPM), or the Search box to filter by name/email/phone. 3. Adjust the Show N entries selector and pager (Page N of M) to page through practices when assigned to many. 4. Click the eye icon in the Action column to open the practice detail view — subsequent Patient Mgmt, Care Mgmt, and Messages actions run in that practice context.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
What it is. Practice List is the master registry of every practice on the platform (for Super Admin) or every practice assigned to the operator (for Admin). Each row can be drilled into to reveal a tabbed practice workspace covering the primary contact, staff (Admins/Providers/Caregivers/System Caregivers), Patients, Schedule & Targets, and Import Patients. For Practice Admin, Provider, and Practice Caregiver, there is no list to browse — the account is bound to a single practice and the Dashboard opens directly into that practice’s tab strip. For System Caregiver, the equivalent screen is the read-only Practices List (Section 5.6).
Why it exists. It is the entry point for every practice-scoped administrative action: adding staff, enrolling patients, configuring monitoring targets, and (for Super Admin) provisioning a brand-new practice via Enrollment (Section 8).
Navigation. - Super Admin: Sidebar → (default landing) or Sidebar → Practice. - Admin: Sidebar → Dashboard → Practice List table → eye icon on a row. - Practice Admin / Provider: Login → Dashboard (auto-opens the one assigned practice). - Practice Caregiver: Login → Dashboard (lands directly on the practice’s patient roster; no separate Practice tab). - System Caregiver: Sidebar → Practice → eye icon on a row.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
Purpose. Locate a specific practice from the master list.
Procedure: 1. Open the Practice List (default landing view for Super Admin; Dashboard table for Admin). 2. Use the Search box to filter by practice name (Admin’s version also filters by email/phone and adds Status, Locations, Patient Range, and Programs dropdowns). 3. Sort by clicking any column header (Status, Practice, Total Patients, Program Enrolled). 4. Click the eye icon on a row to open the practice detail (Practice tab first).
UI Reference — Practice List grid:
Field / Control | Description
Status | Active / Inactive badge for the practice.
Practice | Practice display name (sortable).
Total Patients | Enrolled patient count across all programs.
Program Enrolled | Programs the practice runs with per-program patient counts (e.g., RPM (30), CCM (12)).
Actions | Eye = open detail; Import = open Import Patients directly from the list row.
System Caregiver’s version additionally shows Email, Phone 1, Phone 2, Address, Fax columns and an All Programs filter, but no Add/Edit/Delete controls (read-only).

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
task: 6.3. Practice Tab (Primary Contact, Program Dates, Monitoring Details)
text:
Purpose. Review a practice’s primary contact information, status, program dates, and monitoring configuration.
Access Path. Practice List → eye icon → Practice tab (default tab in the practice detail workspace for every role).
What’s on screen: - Primary Contact card: Facility, Email, Phone 1, Phone 2, Fax, Status (Active shown in green / Inactive in red). - Program Dates table: Program, Start date, End date, Days — one row per enrolled program (CCM and/or RPM). - Monitoring Details panel: flags including “Do you want eVitals to Monitor your patients” and “Buying Device” (Yes = practice purchases devices outright; No = eVitals leases devices for the program), plus the vital categories being monitored (Blood Pressure, Blood Glucose, Weight).
Procedure (illustrative — Admin narrative; identical read for other roles): 1. Confirm the Practice tab is selected (it is the default landing tab). 2. Read the Primary Contact block: Facility, Email, Phone 1, Phone 2, Fax, Status. 3. Review the Program Dates table for each enrolled program. 4. Scroll to Monitoring Details to confirm whether eVitals is monitoring the patients, which vitals are tracked, and whether devices are bought or leased.
Role differences: - Super Admin and Admin can edit contact, program dates, and manage Practice Admins from this workspace (Admin cannot delete a practice; Super Admin deactivates rather than deletes). - Practice Admin, Provider, and Practice Caregiver see this tab as fully read-only — practice contact and monitoring details are managed by Super Admin/Admin only. - A red Status pill (Inactive) blocks new device orders, uploads, and billing until reactivated. Status = Active means the practice is billable in the current cycle; Inactive suppresses new billing events. The “Days” column in Program Dates is the length of the current billing-cycle window, not the days remaining in it.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
Purpose. See and provision every Practice Admin attached to a practice.
Navigation. Practice detail → Admins tab.
What’s on screen. A table of admins: Status chip (A = Active, I = Inactive), Name, Address, Home Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email, plus per-row Action icons (view/edit/delete).
Procedure: 1. Open the Admins tab. 2. Search or filter by All Status to locate an admin. 3. Sort by any column header. 4. Click + Add Practice Admin (top-right); fill in Name, Address, Home Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email and Username, set the initial Status (typically Active), then Save. 5. Use the View (eye), Edit (pencil), Delete (trash) icons in the Action column to manage existing rows. 6. Click Event Logs at the bottom of the table to audit changes to admin records.
Business rules / notes. Deleting the last Active admin is blocked to prevent lock-out. Email must be unique across eVitals — reusing an address is blocked.
Role differences. Super Admin, Admin, and Practice Admin can View/Add/Edit/Delete. Provider sees this tab read-only (view details, no create/edit/delete). Practice Caregiver and System Caregiver do not have an Admins tab at all.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
Purpose. See and register every provider (physician/NP) attached to the practice; these are the billing/signing clinicians that must exist before patients can be assigned to them.
Navigation. Practice detail → Providers tab.
What’s on screen. Table with Status, Name, Address, Home Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email, and Action icons.
Procedure: 1. Open the Providers tab. 2. Search or filter by All Status. 3. Sort by column headers. 4. Click + Add Providers (top-right); enter Name, credentials, NPI, Address, Home Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email, Username, set Status, then Save. 5. Use view/edit/delete icons per row. 6. Open Event Logs for a change history.
Business rules / notes. Providers must exist before patients can be assigned to them (see Patient enrollment, Section 9.2). Provider email drives system notifications (missed uploads, follow-ups) and must be unique.
Role differences. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin can fully manage this roster. Provider can also Add/Edit/Delete on the peer roster (this is documented distinctly in Provider’s role table as Yes/Yes/Yes/Yes for “Providers (peer roster)”). Practice Caregiver and System Caregiver do not have a Providers tab.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
Purpose. See and provision every Caregiver employed directly by the practice — distinct from System Caregivers, who are shared across practices.
Navigation. Practice detail → Caregivers tab.
What’s on screen. Table of caregivers: Status, Name, Address, Home Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email, Action icons; the selected row is highlighted in light blue.
Procedure: 1. Open the Caregivers tab. 2. Search/filter/sort as with Admins and Providers. 3. Click a row (or the eye icon) to view the caregiver’s profile. 4. Click + Add Caregiver (top-right); fill in Name, Address, Home Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email, Username, set Status, then Save.
Business rules / notes. These are practice-employed caregivers, distinct from System Caregivers (Section 10). Caregivers can be scheduled via the Calendar module once created.
Role differences. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin: full Add/Edit/Delete. Provider: view + add (“+ Add Caregiver” available), but Edit is No and Delete is No on this tab for Provider — the screen is read-only for edit/delete purposes despite Add being available (as documented in Provider’s Caregivers-tab privileges box). Practice Caregiver and System Caregiver do not have a Caregivers tab (a Practice Caregiver is this role, not a manager of it).

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
Purpose. Get a vitals-first view of the practice’s patients with device readings, upload status, and CPT billing counters; inspect CCM patients (chronic conditions, service time) and RPM patients (latest vitals) via a toggle.
Navigation. Practice detail → Patients tab.
What’s on screen — Summary cards (five, Practice Admin/Provider/Practice Caregiver view): Total Patient (with A/P/L chips), Recent Uploads (last 24 hours), Missed Uploads (older than 24 hours, sometimes described as “more than 2 days” in the Practice Caregiver dashboard), Abnormal Readings (needs review), CPT Billing (per-code counts with target ratios, e.g., 99453 / 99445 / 99454 “+4 more”). RPM Billing Dates range shown top-right, reflecting the practice’s active RPM contract window.
Patient table columns (CCM view): DOB, Chronic Conditions (coded conditions justifying CCM enrollment), Service Time (minutes accrued in the current billing cycle), Billing (In Progress / Ready / Billed).
Patient table columns (RPM view): Status, Vitals badges (BP/WT/BG), Name, Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse, Glucose, Weight, Last Upload, # Readings, Time, Actions.
Procedure: 1. Open the Patients tab. 2. Review summary/KPI cards; click “click to view all” under any card to drill in. 3. Review CPT Billing counters. 4. Search patients by name, or filter by All Status; use the CCM/RPM toggle at the top-right of the grid to switch program view. 5. Click the eye icon to inspect (open patient dashboard), the pencil icon to edit demographics, or the trash icon (where exposed) to remove a patient row. 6. Click + Add Patient to enroll a new patient (Section 9.2).
Business rules / notes. Sorting by the latest-reading column helps spot coverage gaps — patients who have stopped uploading. The RPM billing date range shown top-right reflects the practice’s current RPM program window.
Role differences. Super Admin/Admin/Practice Admin: full View/Add/Edit/Delete. Provider: View/Add/Edit = Yes, Delete = No. Practice Caregiver: View/Add/Edit = Yes (via the practice dashboard’s own patient grid), Delete = No.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text:
Purpose. See which platform-level (shared) System Caregivers currently serve the practice. This tab is always read-only for adding/editing/removing — those actions live in the standalone System Caregivers module (Section 10), managed by Super Admin/Admin.
Navigation. Practice detail → System Caregivers tab.
What’s on screen. Table with #, Status, Name, Address, Phone, Cell Phone, Fax, Email, Action; empty state reads “No system caregivers found.”
Procedure: 1. Open the System Caregivers tab. 2. Search/filter/sort. 3. If the tab is empty, assign a caregiver from Sidebar → Caregivers (Super Admin/Admin only) — Practice Admin/Provider/Practice Caregiver cannot add or remove System Caregivers from here. 4. Open Event Logs to review assignment history.
Business rules / notes. Calendar access for a System Caregiver is granted separately under Settings → Calendar Permission (Section 17.4), independent of this roster tab.

module: 6. Practice List and the Practice Detail Workspace
text: See Section 9.4 (Import Patients / Bulk Patient Upload) for the complete workflow — the tab is reached at Practice detail → Import Patients and is functionally identical across Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, and Provider (all can View/Add; none can Edit or Delete from this tab). Practice Caregiver and System Caregiver do not have this tab.

module: 7. Enrollment — Add and Configure a Practice (Super Admin only)
text:
What it is / why it exists. Enrollment is where brand-new practices are provisioned on eVitals. A single scrollable form captures Practice Detail, Admin Detail, Practice Settings, and Care Program Billing Cycles in one save. This is the only way a new practice is created on the platform.
Who uses it. Super Admin exclusively. No other role can create a practice (Admin’s Practice List Add = No; Practice Admin/Provider/Practice Caregiver/System Caregiver have no equivalent capability).
Navigation. Sidebar → Enrollment → + Add Practice.
Preconditions. You have the practice’s tax ID, primary address, and the intended admin’s email.
Outcome. A new practice appears in the Practice List; the admin receives a welcome email.
Complete workflow: 1. Navigate to Sidebar → Enrollment → + Add Practice. 2. Fill Practice Detail: name, type, status, tax ID, email, address. 3. Fill Admin Detail: first/last name, email, phone, username, password (meeting live-validated strength criteria), 2FA toggle. 4. Under Practice Settings, review the password-criteria display (length, case, digit, symbol rules shown live under the password field), turn the 2FA toggle on if every admin sign-in should require an emailed OTP, and choose which Email Notification preferences the practice should receive (enrollment, billing, and alert emails). 5. Under Care Program Billing Cycles, set the RPM Start Date and cycle length in days (the End Date is computed automatically); repeat for CCM if the practice will run that program. 6. Click Save to persist the practice and its billing cycles.
UI Reference — Practice Settings:
Field / Control | Description
Password Criteria | Length, case, digit, and symbol requirements enforced live (exact numeric thresholds not specified in the user guide).
2FA | Toggle to require OTP on every sign-in for the admin.
Email Notifications | Toggles for enrollment, billing, and alert emails.
UI Reference — Care Program Billing Cycles:
Field / Control | Description
Start Date | First day of the billing cycle for that program (RPM and/or CCM, entered separately).
Days | Cycle length (e.g., 30).
End Date | Auto-computed from Start Date + Days.
Save / Cancel | Persist the practice or discard.
Privileges. View: Yes. Add: Yes (+ Add Practice creates the practice and its primary contact). Edit: Yes (update practice settings and billing-cycle dates, then Save). Delete: No — practices are deactivated, not deleted, from the UI.
Cross-module relationship. The RPM/CCM Start Date and Days set here become the practice-wide default billing cycle referenced throughout Billing Management (Section 14) and every Lookup Patient (by RPM/CCM date) report (Section 9.3).

module: 8. Platform/Organization-Level Rosters: System Admins and System Caregivers
text:
What it is / why it exists. The master list of every organization-level administrator (Admin/System Admin role) on the platform, letting the Super Admin inspect coverage — how many practices each Admin oversees — and add new Admins.
Navigation. Sidebar → Admins.
Procedure: 1. Click Admins in the left sidebar. 2. Use the search box, or click a column header to sort the roster. 3. Check the Number of Practices column to see how much each admin oversees. 4. Use the row action icon to view or edit the admin’s details.
UI Reference:
Field / Control | Description
Status | Active / Inactive badge.
Name | Admin’s full name.
Address | Business address.
Contact Info | Email and phone.
Number of Practices | Practices linked to this admin.
Privileges. View: Yes. Add: Yes (+ Add Admin creates a system Admin account). Edit: Yes (pencil icon updates profile and scope). Delete: Yes (trash icon removes the Admin account).

module: 8. Platform/Organization-Level Rosters: System Admins and System Caregivers
task: 8.2. System Caregiver Module — Platform Roster (Super Admin / Admin)
text:
What it is / why it exists. System Caregivers are eVitals-employed caregivers shareable across practices. This module is the platform-level roster from which they are created, viewed, edited, and deleted — distinct from the read-only “System Caregivers” tab seen inside an individual practice (Section 6.8).
Navigation. Sidebar → Caregivers.
Procedure — inspect the pool: 1. Click Caregivers in the left sidebar. 2. Filter the roster by name, email, or status. 3. Check which practices each shared caregiver currently serves.
Procedure — maintain the pool: 1. Click + Add Caregiver, then complete First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Username, and Password. 2. Select every practice the caregiver will serve, then click Save. 3. Click the eye icon on a row to open the read-only caregiver profile. 4. Click the pencil icon, change the required fields, click Update. 5. Click the trash icon and confirm the prompt; the caregiver is unassigned from every practice.
Business rules / notes. Setting Status = Inactive preserves the record but prevents sign-in and removes the caregiver from selectable lists on new assignments. Email changes trigger a verification email if two-factor authentication is enabled. Prefer Inactive over Delete when the caregiver has historical patient interactions — deletion is irreversible. Rows shown here are caregivers pooled across practices; practice-scoped (employed) caregivers appear under Practice detail → Caregivers instead (Section 6.6).
Privileges. View: Yes. Add: Yes. Edit: Yes. Delete: Yes.

What it is / why it exists. Patient Management is the workspace for finding and enrolling patients. Depending on role, it is reached either as a standalone cross-practice sidebar module (Super Admin, Admin, System Caregiver — “Patient Mgmt”) or as a practice-scoped flyout with an Add option (Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver). It exposes up to four workflows: Add New Patient / Enroll Patient, Lookup Patient (general), Lookup Patient (by RPM date), and Lookup Patient (by CCM date).
Role differences in what’s exposed: - Super Admin, Admin: three lookups (no Add New Patient listed under the Patient Management module itself in the source’s role table for these two roles — new patients are added from the practice-level Patients tab, Section 6.7, for these roles; Super Admin’s own Patient Management role-privileges row states Add = Yes in the narrative text of 12.7, but the role-privileges-at-a-glance table for Super Admin lists Patient Management as View=No/Add=No/Edit=No/Delete=No — see Section 24 for this discrepancy). - Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver: four options — Add New Patient plus the three lookups. - System Caregiver: three lookups only, no Add New Patient (enrollment is performed by practice-level roles).

task: 9.2. Enroll / Add New Patient — the Three-Step Wizard
text:
What it is. A modal wizard titled “Let’s enroll the patient,” used to enroll a new patient into a practice with demographics, care-team assignment, program selection (CCM and/or RPM), device/meter mapping, and insurance. The wizard only creates the patient record once the final step is submitted (or, per Practice Admin’s narrative, once Save Patient is clicked at the end).
Who can perform it. Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver. (Import Patients — Section 9.4 — is the bulk alternative and is additionally available to Super Admin and Admin at the practice level.)
Navigation. Sidebar/flyout → Patient Mgmt → Add New Patient (Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver); or the practice dashboard’s + Add Patient button (Practice Caregiver dashboard, Patients tab).
Preconditions. The patient’s identity, contact details, an assigned Provider, at least one assigned practice Caregiver, and — for RPM enrollment — meter serial numbers and insurance details, must be on hand. The Provider has the patient’s consent to enroll them.
Outcome. The patient is saved and appears in the Patients grid with status Active and the enrolled program badges (CCM/RPM); CPT counters begin accruing from the RPM/CCM Start Date. The wizard closes with a success confirmation.

task: 9.2. Enroll / Add New Patient — the Three-Step Wizard
text:
Purpose. Capture the patient’s personal information, account credentials, care-team assignments, address, and communication preferences.
Fields (Personal Information):
Field | Required | Notes
Title | No | Mr / Mrs / Ms / Dr / —
First Name | Yes
Middle Name | No
Last Name | Yes
Gender | Yes
Date Of Birth | Yes | mm/dd/yyyy
SSN | Yes | Mask 000-00-0000; stored encrypted at rest, only the last four digits shown in the UI after saving.
Home Phone | Yes
Cell Phone | Yes
Fax | No
Fields (Account Credentials): Username (system proposes one; can be adjusted), Email, initial/temporary Password (patient is prompted to change it on first login).
Fields (Address): Street, City, State, Zip Code (required), Time Zone (required; defaults to UTC-4 with DST (BR) in one role’s documented default, or is otherwise set to the practice’s local zone so reminders arrive at the correct local time).
Fields (Care Team & Settings): Status (Active/Inactive, required), Two Way Authentication (Enabled/Disabled, required), Mobile App Access (Off/On), Provider (required; defaults to the signed-in Provider where the actor is a Provider), optional System Caregiver, at least one Practice Caregiver (required — the form blocks Next with “Select at least one practice caregiver” until this is filled, even for RPM-only enrollments, because this caregiver is responsible for reviewing uploads), optional Upload Picture (max 1 MB), Preferred Language, SMS/Email notification toggles.
Business rules: First Name, Last Name, Gender, Date of Birth, SSN, Home Phone, and Cell Phone are required — Next stays disabled until all are valid. Practice Caregiver is a hard requirement even for RPM-only enrollments.

task: 9.2. Enroll / Add New Patient — the Three-Step Wizard
text:
Purpose. Enroll the patient into CCM, RPM, or both; choose chronic conditions; and set the care-plan cadence.
Procedure: 1. Toggle CCM to enroll in Chronic Care Management. If CCM is on, pick two or more Chronic Conditions from the list — a minimum of two is required for CPT 99490 billing. Choose the Care Plan Type (Standard / Complex) and the review cadence. 2. Toggle RPM to enroll in Remote Patient Monitoring. If RPM is on, pick the vitals to monitor — Blood Pressure, Blood Glucose, Weight (at least one required). Each ticked vital shows a chip on the Patients grid. 3. Click Next to advance to Step 3 (RPM) when RPM is enabled, or Save/finish if only CCM is enabled.
Business rules: At least one program (CCM or RPM) must be enabled to proceed. Chronic Conditions can be added or removed later from the patient profile without unenrolling the patient. The RPM vital selection determines which target sets apply — BP uses Systolic/Diastolic/Pulse targets, Glucose uses meal-time targets, Weight uses Weight/BMI targets (all configured under Schedule & Targets, Section 11). The wizard adds a matching RPM and/or CCM step at the top of the stepper for each selected program; the CCM step only appears when CCM is ticked.

task: 9.2. Enroll / Add New Patient — the Three-Step Wizard
subtask: 9.2.3. Step 3 — RPM Device & Insurance (only if RPM was selected)
text:
Purpose. Bind the patient’s device/meter(s) to their record and capture insurance details required for RPM billing.
Procedure: 1. For each selected vital, choose the Meter Model (Model Number as printed on the device). 2. Enter the Meter Serial Number — exactly 16 characters; the field validates length and uniqueness, and the form disables Save Patient / Next until the length matches. A serial number already bound to another patient is rejected — the meter must be unassigned first. 3. Optionally enter a Gateway Serial Number for a cellular hub. 4. Click the + icon to add another meter row (for multiple devices/vitals). 5. Set the RPM Start Date (required) — this drives the billing window and the CPT 99453 setup claim; the Practice tab’s Program Dates table reflects it immediately. 6. Enter Primary Insurance (Carrier/Insurance Name, Subscriber Id/Member ID, Insured’s Name, Group No., Plan Type) and, if applicable, Secondary Insurance below it. 7. Capture the Patient Consent method (Verbal / Written) and consent date. 8. Click Save Patient to finish the wizard. Use Previous/Back to return to earlier steps, or Cancel to discard the draft.
Business rules: For dual-program (CCM+RPM) patients, the CCM enrollment date is captured separately on Step 2 — the two programs bill on independent cycles. Two-Way Authentication and Mobile App Access can be edited later from the patient profile. RPM Start Date sets the beginning of the current 30-day billing window (30 days is the length observed in the documented example; the general default cycle length is configured at the practice level per Section 7).

task: 9.2. Enroll / Add New Patient — the Three-Step Wizard
text: The stepper across the top (Demographics · Programs · RPM · CCM) shows filled steps as blue check marks and the current step as a highlighted ring. Cancel discards the draft entirely; a saved patient (once Save Patient succeeds) is removed from the Patients grid only via the normal delete action, not via Cancel.

Purpose. Find a patient by name, practice, provider, caregiver, and/or status.
Navigation. Patient Mgmt (sidebar or flyout) → Lookup Patient.
Fields / filters: Last Name, First Name, Practice (defaults to the current practice for a Practice Admin; a required filter labeled “Program Enrolled” for Provider/Practice Caregiver/System Caregiver variants of this screen), Provider, Caregiver, Status (Active / Paused / Lost, or “—- Select —-” for all).
Procedure: 1. Enter any combination of filters. 2. Click Query to run the search (some role variants require Program Enrolled to be selected before Query is enabled); use Reset to clear all filters. 3. Use the top-right Search box to keyword-filter the loaded result set further. 4. Click a column header (e.g., Name) to sort. 5. Click a patient row/name to open the patient dashboard.
Results grid columns: #, Status, Vitals chips (BP/BG/WT — showing which measurement types are being monitored), Name, Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse, Glucose, Weight, Last Upload, # Readings, Time.
Business rules / notes: Leaving all filters blank returns an empty grid; at least one filter (or the required Program Enrolled filter, depending on role) must be supplied before Query runs. Practice Admins can only search within their own practice — the Practice dropdown is scoped accordingly. This screen shows the latest vital readings; for date-scoped billing views use the RPM-date or CCM-date lookups below. Empty state text: “Select filters and click Query to load patients.”

Purpose. Report RPM service activity for a practice over a chosen date range, including live CPT eligibility.
Navigation. Patient Mgmt → Lookup Patient (by RPM date).
Fields / filters: Practice (where applicable to the role), RPM Service Date Range (From ~ To, mm/dd/yyyy pickers).
Procedure: 1. Select a Practice (if applicable). 2. Pick the RPM Service Date Range. 3. Click Query to load results, or Reset to clear. 4. Sort by RPM Start Date (default) or any other column. 5. Distribute via Print, Export (CSV/Excel), or Email.
Results grid columns: #, Status, Vitals, Patient Name, DOB, Model # (also spelled “Modal #” in some screenshots), Serial #, RPM Start Date, Upload Date/Time, Measurement Days, Service Time, Caregiver, Provider, Eligible CPT Codes.
Business rules / notes: - Measurement Days counts unique calendar days with at least one qualifying vital upload in the window — this is the direct driver of CPT 99454 eligibility (16 or more measurement days required per the CCM/RPM chapter’s cross-reference — see Section 13.2 for the exact rule). - Service Time is the accumulated caregiver-review time in the window — the driver for CPT 99457/99458. - Model # and Serial # show the device model and serial actively assigned during the reporting window; a dash in either field means the meter binding is not complete — this must be fixed on the patient profile before billing. - Eligible CPT Codes is a live calculation across 99453 (setup), 99454 (device supply), 99457 (first 20 minutes), and 99458 (each additional 20 minutes). Rows displaying “–” are not yet eligible for any code.

Purpose. Report CCM service activity for a practice over a chosen date range with chronic conditions and billing status.
Navigation. Patient Mgmt → Lookup Patient (by CCM date).
Fields / filters: Practice (where applicable), CCM Service Date Range (From ~ To).
Procedure: 1. Select a Practice (if applicable). 2. Pick the CCM Service Date Range. 3. Click Query to load results, or Reset to clear. 4. Sort by Enrollment Date (default) or any other column. 5. Distribute via Print, Export, or Email.
Results grid columns: #, Status, Patient Name, DOB, Chronic Conditions, Enrollment Date, Last Activity, Service Time, Eligible CPT Codes, Billing (Pending / Billed / Locked, depending on role’s phrasing).
Business rules / notes: - Chronic Conditions lists every ICD-coded condition captured on the CCM enrollment step — at least two are required for CPT 99490 billing. - Billing = Pending means the current cycle has not yet been submitted; Billed means the claim has been filed for the window; Locked (per the Billing Management module’s phrasing) means billing has already been finalized. - Eligible CPT Codes on this report reflects CPT 99490 (first 20 minutes), 99439 (each additional 20 minutes), and 99491 (physician-provided CCM), based on Service Time and provider type.

The following fields recur across the enrollment wizard, patient grids, and billing/lookup reports. This consolidated list exists so a single retrieval can answer “what does field X mean” without needing the originating screen.
Field | Meaning | Where it appears
DOB | Date of birth | Patients tab, Lookup reports
Chronic Conditions | ICD-coded diagnoses justifying CCM enrollment; ≥2 required for CPT 99490 | Patients tab (CCM view), CCM lookup report, enrollment wizard Step 2
Service Time | Minutes of caregiver/provider interaction accrued in the current billing cycle | Patients tab, RPM/CCM lookup reports, Billing reports
Billing (status) | In Progress / Ready / Billed / Pending / Locked, depending on screen | Patients tab, Billing Management, Lookup reports
Vitals chips | BP / BG / WT badges showing which measurement types are being monitored for the patient | Patients tab, Lookup Patient results
Systolic / Diastolic / Pulse | Latest blood-pressure and heart-rate reading | Patients tab (RPM view), Lookup Patient results
Glucose | Latest blood-glucose reading | Patients tab (RPM view), Lookup Patient results
Weight | Latest weight reading | Patients tab (RPM view), Lookup Patient results
Model # / Serial # | The device model and the 16-character serial number actively assigned to the patient | RPM lookup report, Inventory mapped-device table
RPM Start Date | Date RPM enrollment began; anchors the billing window and CPT 99453 setup claim | Enrollment wizard Step 3, RPM lookup report, Practice tab Program Dates
Upload Date/Time | Timestamp of the most recent device upload in the queried window | RPM lookup report
Measurement Days | Count of unique days with a qualifying upload in the window; drives CPT 99454 | RPM lookup report
Eligible CPT Codes | System-calculated list of CPT codes the patient currently qualifies for | RPM/CCM lookup reports, Billing reports
Enrollment Date | Date the patient’s CCM enrollment began | CCM lookup report
Last Activity | Most recent recorded CCM-relevant activity | CCM lookup report

What it is / why it exists. Add multiple patients to a practice in a single upload by supplying a CSV/Excel file mapped to a chosen Provider and Caregiver, avoiding one-by-one manual enrollment.
Who can perform it. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider (all View=Yes, Add=Yes, Edit=No, Delete=No for this tab). Practice Caregiver and System Caregiver do not have this capability.
Navigation. Practice List → row → Import icon; or Practice detail → Import Patients tab → “Add Bulk Patients.”
Preconditions. At least one Provider and one Caregiver exist on the practice; the CSV/Excel file follows the eVitals bulk-import template (patient demographics, contact, program assignment).
Outcome. Valid rows create new patient records assigned to the selected Provider and Caregiver; invalid rows are reported back with a row-level error list.
Fields:
Field | Required | Notes
Provider | Yes | Dropdown of active providers; every imported patient is attached to this provider as ordering clinician.
Caregiver | Yes | Dropdown of active caregivers; every imported patient is attached to this caregiver for monitoring.
CSV / Excel File | Yes | .csv, .xls, .xlsx; must use the eVitals bulk template — download the sample from the help tooltip if the practice has never imported before.
Procedure: 1. Open the practice and click the Import Patients tab. 2. Choose a Provider from the dropdown. 3. Choose a Caregiver from the second dropdown. 4. Click Upload CSV/Excel and select the prepared file — the chosen filename replaces the “No file chosen” placeholder. 5. Click Import Patients (or Import) to start processing. A confirmation toast reports how many rows succeeded and how many failed. 6. If failures are reported, download the error file, correct the flagged rows, and re-upload only the corrected subset. 7. Click Cancel to abandon the import before submission.
Business rules / notes: - Provider and Caregiver selections apply to every row in the file — split the file if patients need different assignments. - The importer is idempotent by MRN; a duplicate MRN row is skipped rather than creating a second patient. - Program-enrollment columns in the file (CCM/RPM start dates) must fall within the practice’s active billing cycle or the row is rejected.

System Caregivers are documented in three places in the source manual, consolidated here for retrieval convenience:
Platform roster (create/edit/delete) — Super Admin / Admin only, Sidebar → Caregivers. See Section 8.2.
Practice-level assignment view (read-only) — every practice-scoped role sees a “System Caregivers” tab showing which shared caregivers currently serve that practice, but cannot add/edit/remove from that tab. See Section 6.8.
The System Caregiver’s own workspace — when a System Caregiver signs in, they see the Practices List (Section 5.6) and practice-scoped lookups (Sections 9.3–9.5) for their assigned practices only.
Calendar and Chat access for System Caregivers are granted separately, per practice or per Provider, via Settings → Calendar Permission (Section 17.4) and Settings → Chat Access (Section 17.5) — assignment to a practice alone does not grant calendar visibility or messaging rights; those are explicit, additional grants.

What it is / why it exists. Schedule & Targets defines the practice’s default daily anchor times and, per vital type, the reading windows and normal/target ranges used to classify incoming RPM readings as in-range or abnormal. Configuring this module correctly is what allows the Patients grid, Follow Up Query, and alerting to flag out-of-range readings — the source manual is explicit that no clinical interpretation beyond what is configured here should be assumed (see Section 20 on vitals/readings for the corresponding caution about UI color-coding).
Who uses it. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin all have View=Yes, Add=Not applicable (targets are configured, not created as new records), Edit=Yes, Delete=No (targets cannot be deleted — they are reset to default values instead) — this applies to Daily Schedule, Blood Pressure, Blood Glucose, and Weight sub-tabs alike.
Navigation. Practice detail → Schedule & Targets tab, with four sub-tabs: Daily Schedule, Blood Pressure, Blood Glucose, Weight. Daily Schedule is selected by default.

Purpose. Set the practice’s default daily anchor times (Wake-up, Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Bed) that anchor every other reading window.
Fields and defaults: Wake-Up (default 06:00 AM), Breakfast (08:00 AM), Lunch (12:00 PM), Dinner (06:00 PM), Bed (10:00 PM). All five anchor times are required (marked with a red asterisk).
Procedure: 1. Open Schedule & Targets; Daily Schedule is selected by default. 2. Set Wake-up, Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, and Bed times using the five labeled cards/pickers. 3. Click Save to apply, or Cancel to discard. 4. Click Event Logs to review prior schedule changes.
Business rules: Changes take effect for readings uploaded after the save; historical readings retain their original window.

Purpose. Define five measurement windows (Wake-up, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening) and their target Systolic, Diastolic, and Pulse ranges — each row combines the reading window with its target range in one place.
Fields and defaults (per window, identical defaults across all five windows unless the practice edits them): Systolic Pressure min–max: default 100–130. Diastolic Pressure min–max: default 50–80. Pulse min–max: default 60–100.
Procedure: 1. Click the Blood Pressure sub-tab. 2. For each of the five periods (Wake-up, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening), set the Reading Window (Start–End time). 3. Enter Systolic, Diastolic, and Pulse target ranges for that period. 4. Click Save, or Cancel to revert. Use Event Logs to audit prior values.
Business rules: Reading windows should not overlap across bands — validation flags any conflicts before Save is accepted. Systolic, Diastolic, or Pulse readings outside the configured targets are flagged as abnormal in the Patients grid and render in red, triggering Abnormal Readings alerts.

Purpose. Define reading windows and target glucose ranges for each of nine periods across the day, listed as one scannable table ordered from wake-up through midnight.
Periods (nine, in order): Wake-up Time, Before-Breakfast, After-Breakfast, Before-Lunch, After-Lunch, Before-Dinner, After-Dinner, Bedtime, Midnight.
Fields and defaults: Fasting-style windows (e.g., Wake-up, Before-meal) default to 60–110 mg/dL; post-meal windows (After-Breakfast, After-Lunch, After-Dinner) default to 70–140 mg/dL.
Procedure: 1. Click the Blood Glucose sub-tab. 2. For each of the nine rows, set the Reading Window (Start–End) and the Target Range (mg/dL) side by side. 3. Click Save; use Cancel to discard or Event Logs to view history.
Business rules: All BG window fields are required (marked with red asterisks). Windows are chronological — a Before-Lunch start time earlier than the Lunch anchor set in Daily Schedule is rejected. Adjacent windows chain end→start (e.g., After-Breakfast end = Before-Lunch start).

Purpose. Set the recommended weight, body-fat, BMI, and daily time-window targets used to classify each patient’s weight readings.
Preconditions. The practice is enrolled in RPM with a weight-scale program; the patient’s baseline weight, height, and body composition are known (for the auto-derived “Recommended” fields to populate meaningfully).
Outcome. Saved thresholds drive out-of-range alerts and color coding on the patient vitals dashboard. Changes take effect on the next weight reading uploaded from the paired scale.
Field reference:
Field | Required | Description / Notes
Recommended Weight Range | Auto (read-only) | Guideline in lb, calculated from patient demographics; refreshes only after the patient profile (height, age, sex) is updated.
Recommended Body Fat Range | Auto (read-only) | Guideline in %, calculated from patient profile.
Weight Target Range | Yes | Two numeric inputs (lower–upper) in lb. Default 66–220 lb. Accepts one decimal place; UI validates lower < upper. Values outside this range trigger an out-of-range flag on the patient chart.
Body Fat Target Range | Yes | Two numeric inputs (lower–upper) in %. Default 14–27%.
BMI Reference — Underweight | Auto (read-only) | Fixed clinical reference band: BMI < 18.5.
BMI Reference — Normal | Auto (read-only) | Fixed clinical reference band: BMI 18.5–24.9.
BMI Reference — Overweight | Auto (read-only) | Fixed clinical reference band: BMI 25.0–29.9.
BMI Reference — Obese | Auto (read-only) | Fixed clinical reference band: BMI ≥ 30.0. Values in this band are classified obese.
Morning window | Yes | Start–end time for morning weigh-ins. Default 06:00 AM – 03:59 PM.
Afternoon window | Yes | Start–end time. Default 12:00 PM – 09:59 PM.
Evening window | Yes | Start–end time. Default 06:00 PM – 09:59 AM (wraps past midnight; the system treats it as an overnight interval).
Procedure: 1. Open the practice, select Schedule & Targets, then click the Weight sub-tab. 2. Confirm the Recommended Weight Range and Recommended Body Fat Range shown as guidance (read-only). 3. Enter the Weight Target Range (lb) and Body Fat Target Range (%) lower/upper bounds. 4. Review the BMI Reference bands (Underweight, Normal, Overweight, Obese) — fixed, not editable. 5. Adjust the Morning, Afternoon, and Evening reading windows under Monitoring Windows if the practice uses non-default weigh-in slots. 6. Click Save to persist, or Cancel to discard. Use Event Logs to review who last edited these values.
Business rules: The BMI Reference bands are fixed clinical reference values and are never editable, unlike Weight Target Range and Body Fat Target Range which are practice-configurable.

task: 11.6. Cross-Module Relationship: How Schedule & Targets Drives Everything Downstream
text: Schedule & Targets is the single source of truth for what counts as an “abnormal” or “out-of-range” reading anywhere else in the platform: - Patients tab / grids (Section 6.7, 9.6): out-of-range Systolic/Diastolic/Pulse, Glucose, or Weight values render in red/amber and populate the “Abnormal Readings” summary card. - Follow Up Query (Section 15): out-of-range readings and missed uploads (relative to the configured windows) are among the triggers that surface a patient in the outreach work-list. - Weight target changes take effect only on the next uploaded reading from the paired scale — historical readings are not retroactively reclassified when targets change (documented explicitly for Daily Schedule and implied for the other sub-tabs by the same “changes take effect after save” language).

What it is / why it exists. Inventory catalogues the connected devices eVitals ships to patients — blood-pressure monitors, scales, glucometers. It tracks catalogue products in bulk (by Model Number, price, quantity, status) and individual physical units by Serial Number, and shows which patient (if any) each unit is currently assigned to.
Who uses it. Super Admin and Admin only (View/Add/Edit/Delete = Yes for both). Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, and System Caregiver have no Inventory module — device binding for their patients happens through the patient enrollment wizard (Section 9.2.3), which draws on this same underlying serial-number pool.
Navigation. Sidebar → Inventory.

What’s on screen. Columns: #, Product Name, Product Category, Model Number, Received Date, Price, Qty, Status, Action.
Procedure: 1. Click Inventory in the left sidebar. 2. Search/filter by product name, category, or model number. 3. Sort by clicking any column header (e.g., Received Date, Price, Qty). 4. Page through with the pager or Show-entries selector. 5. Click Event Logs (bottom) to audit inventory add/edit/delete activity.
UI Reference:
Field / Control | Description
Model Number | Manufacturer model identifier.
Price | Unit price.
Qty | Quantity currently in stock — the total number of individual devices tracked under this product; expand via the eye icon to see per-serial mappings.
Status | Available / Depleted (list view) or Active/Inactive (detail/edit view) — the Status chip (A = Active) means the product is available for assignment; inactive products remain visible for historical reference but cannot be issued to patients.
Action (eye) | Opens Inventory Details for that product.

task: 12.3. Add a Product (Register a New Device Category)
text:
Purpose. Register a new product category (BP monitor, glucose meter, scale, etc.) into the system.
Preconditions. The product category, model number, and initial stock quantity are known.
Outcome. A new inventory row is created and available for serial-number mapping and assignment.
Procedure: 1. Click + Add Inventory (top-right). 2. Fill in Product Category, Product Name, Model Number, Received Date, Price, and Qty of Each Category. 3. Optionally enter a Gateway Serial Number for cellular hubs. 4. Set Status = Active. 5. Click OK to save, or Cancel to discard.
Business rules: Qty determines how many serial numbers can be mapped later under Inventory Details.

task: 12.4. Inventory Details (Trace Individual Devices by Serial Number)
text:
Purpose. Drill into a product to see every individual device serial and its assignment status.
Navigation. Inventory list → eye icon on a product row.
What’s on screen. Header: Product Category, Product Name, Meter Model, Received Date, Price, Qty of Each Category, Status, Gateway Serial Number. Below it, a Mapped Device Table: Product Name, Product Model Number, Product Serial Number, Assignee, Assigning Date.
Procedure: 1. From the Inventory List, click the eye icon on the target product row. 2. Review the header summary. 3. Scroll to Mapped Devices to see the per-device roster. 4. Search or sort to locate a specific serial. 5. Click + Add new meter to register additional serial numbers under this product. 6. Click List (top-right) to return to the Inventory List.
Business rules: - Rows where Assignee = N/A are unassigned devices available for issue; a name plus an Assigning Date means the device is currently allocated to a patient. - Serial numbers created under “+ Add new meter” count toward the product’s Qty of Each Category.

Purpose. Update product-level data such as price, quantity, status, or review the on-file serial numbers.
Navigation. Inventory list → pencil icon → “Edit Products” modal.
Procedure: 1. Click the pencil icon on the target inventory row. 2. Update Product Category, Qty of Each Category, Product Name, Received Date, Model Number, Gateway Serial Number, Price, or Status as needed. 3. Review the (read-only) “Serial numbers on file” list at the bottom of the modal. 4. Click OK to save, or Cancel to discard.
Business rules: - Assigned serials cannot be changed from this screen — the modal displays this message explicitly. Use Inventory Details → Mapped device to manage individual devices instead. - Decreasing Qty below the number of already-mapped serials is blocked by validation. - Setting Status = Inactive keeps historical records intact but prevents new assignments.

Purpose. Permanently remove a product from inventory.
Preconditions. No serial numbers under the product are currently assigned to a patient.
Procedure: 1. Click the red trash icon on the target inventory row. 2. Confirm the deletion in the modal.
Business rules: If any mapped device is still assigned, the system blocks deletion — unassign devices first, or mark the product Inactive instead. The deletion is logged in Event Logs.

Rule | Value / Constraint | Where enforced
Meter Serial Number length (patient enrollment) | Exactly 16 characters | Enrollment wizard Step 3 (RPM Device); form disables Save/Next until length matches
Serial Number uniqueness | A serial already bound to another patient is rejected; must be unassigned first | Enrollment wizard Step 3
Gateway Serial Number | Optional, for cellular hub devices | Inventory Add/Edit; optionally at patient meter-mapping
Model Number format | Exactly as printed on the physical device (free text, manufacturer-defined) | Inventory, patient enrollment
Deleting an assigned device | Blocked at both the Inventory-product level (Section 12.6) and implicitly at the individual-serial level (must unassign first) | Inventory module
Qty reduction below mapped-serial count | Blocked by validation | Edit Product modal

task: 12.8. Cross-Module Relationship: Patient ↔ Device ↔ Model ↔ Serial Number ↔ Vital Type ↔ RPM ↔ Measurements ↔ Billing
text:
A Super Admin/Admin creates a Product in Inventory (Model Number, category, price, quantity) and optionally pre-registers individual Serial Numbers under “+ Add new meter.”
During patient enrollment (Section 9.2.3), a Provider/Practice Admin/Practice Caregiver selects a Meter Model and enters a 16-character Serial Number for each RPM vital the patient will be monitored on (BP, Glucose, Weight). This binds that specific physical unit to that specific patient — reflected in the Inventory Details “Mapped Device Table” (Assignee + Assigning Date).
The bound device transmits vital readings, which are evaluated against the practice’s Schedule & Targets (Section 11) reading windows and ranges to determine in-range/abnormal status.
Each qualifying upload contributes to that patient’s Measurement Days count for the current RPM billing cycle.
Caregiver/provider review of those readings and any documented Follow Up contributes to Service Time.
Measurement Days and Service Time are evaluated against CPT code rules (Section 13) to produce the “Eligible CPT Codes” shown on the RPM Lookup report (Section 9.4) and the Billing Management RPM report (Section 14.4).
If a device is unassigned or its Model #/Serial # binding is incomplete (shown as a dash), the RPM lookup report flags this and billing eligibility for that patient is blocked until the binding is fixed.

module: 13. Vital Readings, RPM Monitoring, and Care Management (CCM)
text:
Vital | What it represents | Unit | Associated device | Reading windows configured (Section 11) | Default target range(s)
Blood Pressure (Systolic / Diastolic) + Pulse | Cardiovascular reading captured by a BP cuff | mmHg (BP), bpm (Pulse) | BP monitor/cuff | 5 windows: Wake-up, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening | Systolic 100–130, Diastolic 50–80, Pulse 60–100 (identical defaults per window)
Blood Glucose | Blood sugar level captured by a glucometer | mg/dL | Glucometer | 9 windows: Wake-up, Before/After-Breakfast, Before/After-Lunch, Before/After-Dinner, Bedtime, Midnight | Fasting/before-meal windows 60–110; post-meal windows 70–140
Weight (+ Body Fat, BMI) | Body weight captured by a connected scale, with derived Body Fat % and BMI | lb (weight), % (body fat), BMI unitless | Weight scale | 3 windows: Morning, Afternoon, Evening | Weight 66–220 lb, Body Fat 14–27%; BMI reference bands fixed (Underweight <18.5, Normal 18.5–24.9, Overweight 25.0–29.9, Obese ≥30.0)
On color-coding. The source manual documents that out-of-range Systolic/Diastolic/Pulse readings “render in red on the Patients grid and trigger Abnormal Readings alerts,” and that the Weight module’s saved thresholds “drive out-of-range alerts and colour coding on the patient vitals dashboard.” Beyond red = abnormal / out-of-range, the interface displays color-coded indicators (e.g., amber, status chips), but the user guide does not explicitly define every color’s precise clinical threshold or meaning beyond the ranges configured in Schedule & Targets — no additional clinical interpretation should be inferred.

module: 13. Vital Readings, RPM Monitoring, and Care Management (CCM)
text:
Purpose. RPM is one of the two care programs a patient can be enrolled into (the other is CCM). It centers on connected devices transmitting vitals from the patient’s home, evaluated for billing eligibility.
Enrollment. A patient is enrolled into RPM on Step 2 (Programs) of the enrollment wizard by toggling RPM on and selecting at least one vital to monitor (Section 9.2.2); device binding and the RPM Start Date are captured on Step 3 (Section 9.2.3).
Patient eligibility information stated by the manual. The manual does not state clinical eligibility criteria for RPM (e.g., required diagnoses) — RPM eligibility in the wizard is simply the RPM toggle plus selection of at least one vital type. (Contrast with CCM, which requires ≥2 chronic conditions — Section 13.3.)
Device requirements. At least one device (BP cuff, glucometer, and/or scale) matching the selected vital(s), bound with a valid 16-character Serial Number (Section 12.7).
Monitoring / Measurement Days. Measurement Days = count of unique calendar days with at least one qualifying vital upload within the billing window. The manual explicitly ties this to CPT 99454 eligibility, stating “16 or more days are required” (documented in the Provider chapter’s RPM-lookup Notes).
Service Time. Minutes of caregiver/provider review accrued in the window; drives CPT 99457 (first 20 minutes) and 99458 (each additional 20 minutes).
Readings / Reports. See Section 9.4 (Lookup Patient by RPM Date) and Section 14.4 (Billing Management RPM report) for the exact grid columns.
