Workflow dependencies. RPM billing eligibility depends on: (a) a completed device binding (Model #/Serial #), (b) meeting the Measurement Days threshold, and (c) accrued Service Time — see Section 13.4 for the full CPT rule set.
Relevant statuses. Patient Status (Active/Paused/Lost or Active/Pending/Left, depending on the grid); device Assignee status (assigned vs. N/A/unassigned); billing status (In Progress/Ready/Billed, or Pending/Billed/Locked, depending on screen).
RPM-related errors/warnings. A dash (“–”) in Model # or Serial # on the RPM lookup report signals an incomplete device binding that must be corrected before billing. A serial number already assigned to another patient is rejected at enrollment. Rejected bulk-import rows are reported with row-level errors (Section 9.7).

module: 13. Vital Readings, RPM Monitoring, and Care Management (CCM)
text:
Purpose. CCM is the non-device-centric care program for patients with multiple chronic conditions who receive ongoing care coordination (as opposed to RPM’s device-vitals focus).
Enrollment. Toggled on during Step 2 of the enrollment wizard; requires selecting two or more Chronic Conditions from the list — this minimum of two is explicitly required for CPT 99490 billing eligibility. The Care Plan Type (Standard / Complex) and review cadence are also set on this step.
Care-plan complexity. “Complexity” (Non-Complex / Complex) is shown on the CCM billing report but is not manually entered on that report screen — it reflects the patient’s underlying care-plan configuration set during/after enrollment.
Billing Path. Also shown on the CCM billing report, likewise derived from the care plan rather than typed in on the report; the full enumerated set of Billing Path values is not specified in the user guide.
Service Time / eligible codes. CPT 99490 = first 20 minutes of clinical staff time; CPT 99439 = each additional 20 minutes; CPT 99491 = physician-provided CCM (as opposed to clinical-staff-provided). See Section 13.4.
Reports. See Section 9.5 (Lookup Patient by CCM Date) and Section 14.4 (Billing Management CCM report tab).

module: 13. Vital Readings, RPM Monitoring, and Care Management (CCM)
task: 13.4. Follow Up Query — Identifying Patients Needing Outreach
text:
What it is / why it exists. Care Management’s Follow Up Query surfaces patients whose upload cadence, vitals, or care-plan items need caregiver attention — missed uploads, abnormal readings, or unanswered care-plan items.
Who uses it. Every operator role has View=Yes, Add/Edit/Delete=No — Follow Up records are generated from patient activity, not manually created here. All six operator roles (Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, System Caregiver) can run this query; results are scoped to whatever practices that role can see.
Navigation. Sidebar → Care Mgmt → Follow Up (page title: “Follow Up Query”).
Filters (vary slightly by role): Last Name, First Name, Phone Number (Practice Admin variant); Practice, Provider, Caregiver, Status (Super Admin/Admin variant); Program Enrolled (required for Practice Admin/Provider/Practice Caregiver/System Caregiver variants — the query cannot run without it); DOB.
Procedure: 1. Open Care Mgmt in the sidebar; the page opens as Follow Up Query. 2. Enter any combination of name/phone/DOB filters and pick Practice/Provider/Caregiver/Status/Program Enrolled as available for the role. 3. Click Query to run the search, or Reset to clear filters. 4. Use the top-right Search box to narrow the returned rows further. 5. Sort by clicking the Name (or other) column header. 6. Use the row Action icons/column to open the patient dashboard, log a follow-up call/note/task, or address the flagged item. 7. Distribute via Print, Export, or Email where available.
Results grid columns. #, Status, Vitals chips, Name, Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse, Glucose, Weight, Last Upload, # Readings, Time, Action.
Business rules / notes: - There is no separate Practice filter for Practice-Admin-scoped variants — results are already scoped to the signed-in Practice Admin’s practice. - Dismissing a follow-up here does not delete the underlying missed-upload/abnormal-reading events — it only removes the row from the outreach queue. - Follow-up notes logged here contribute to Service Time on the CCM lookup report. - Follow Up templates (Settings → Follow Up, Section 17.2) are used to standardize documentation when acting on a flagged patient; preconditions for a productive Follow Up Query session include having those templates configured. - Selecting a Caregiver filter narrows to that caregiver’s panel — useful for daily huddles. - Empty state: “Select filters and click Query to load patients.”

What it is / why it exists. Billing rolls up service-time and measurement evidence per practice, per program, per patient, and marks readiness to invoice for the current cycle. It exists so that a practice can prove, code by code, that a patient’s RPM or CCM billing requirements were met before submitting a claim.
Who uses it as a standalone module. Super Admin and Admin only (Billing Management module, sidebar). View=Yes for both; Add/Edit/Delete=No for both — billing rows are system-generated from readings and service time, never hand-entered or edited. Practice Admin, Provider, and Practice Caregiver do not have a separate Billing module, but see the same underlying CPT eligibility surfaced as: (a) the “CPT Billing” summary card and counters on their Patients tab/dashboard (Section 6.7, 5.5), and (b) the Eligible CPT Codes column on their Lookup Patient (by RPM/CCM date) reports (Sections 9.4–9.5).
Navigation. Sidebar → Billing (Super Admin/Admin).

What’s on screen. “Practice List For Billing Report” with columns: ID, Status, Name, Phone 1, Email, Program Enrolled (chip, e.g., “RPM (46)”), Billing Period Date (the current cycle window: start ~ end), Patients Status (four colored chips: T / A / P / L), View Report (eye icon).
T / A / P / L badge meanings: - T = Total patients in the billing period. - A = Active (meeting service-time thresholds). - P = Pending (partial data / awaiting review). - L = Locked (billing already finalized for the cycle).
Zero-count chips are still shown for context (e.g., “L 0” means no billing has been finalized yet for the cycle).
Procedure: 1. Click Billing in the left sidebar. 2. Search by practice name, ID, or email. 3. Sort by Status or any column header. 4. Read the Program Enrolled chip to see how many patients are enrolled in each program for that practice. 5. Click the eye icon in the View Report column to open the per-practice Billing & Reports page (opens on the RPM tab, with a CCM tab alongside). 6. Click the calendar icon to change the billing period date range before generating the report. 7. Adjust Show-entries / pager to page through the practice list. 8. Click Event Logs (top of table) to audit billing activity.

task: 14.3. CPT Code Reference (complete set documented in the source manual)
text:
CPT 99453 — RPM Setup / Patient Education - Description per the manual: the “setup claim” tied to the RPM Start Date captured on the enrollment wizard’s RPM step. - Required conditions: device is bound to the patient and an RPM Start Date is set. - Related workflow: Patient enrollment Step 3 (Section 9.2.3); triggered once at the start of RPM monitoring. - Where it appears: Enrollment wizard notes, CPT Billing summary card, RPM lookup report, Billing Management RPM report. - Which role can view: Any role that can see the CPT Billing card or the relevant report (all six operator roles, scoped to their access).
CPT 99454 — RPM Device Supply / Data Transmission - Description per the manual: billed based on Measurement Days — the count of unique calendar days with at least one qualifying vital upload in the billing window. - Required conditions: 16 or more measurement days in the billing window (stated explicitly in the Provider chapter’s RPM lookup Notes: “it drives CPT 99454 eligibility (16 or more days are required)”). - Related workflow: device transmits readings → Measurement Days accrue → RPM lookup / Billing report shows eligibility. - Where it appears: RPM lookup report (Measurement Days column), Billing Management RPM report, Patients tab CPT Billing card.
CPT 99457 — RPM Treatment Management, First 20 Minutes - Description per the manual: billed based on accrued Service Time — “the driver for CPT 99457 / 99458.” - Required conditions: at least the first 20-minute increment of qualifying caregiver/provider review/interaction time in the billing window. - Related workflow: caregiver reviews readings / documents Follow Up → Service Time accrues. - Where it appears: RPM lookup report (Service Time column), Billing Management RPM report.
CPT 99458 — RPM Treatment Management, Each Additional 20 Minutes - Description per the manual: same Service Time driver as 99457, for each additional 20-minute increment beyond the first. - Where it appears: same reports as 99457, listed as a separate eligible code once the additional-time threshold is met.

task: 14.3. CPT Code Reference (complete set documented in the source manual)
text:
CPT 99490 — CCM Care Coordination, First 20 Minutes (Clinical Staff) - Description per the manual: CCM’s base billing code. - Required conditions: the patient has two or more Chronic Conditions selected on the CCM enrollment step, and at least the first 20-minute increment of clinical-staff CCM service time has been documented (Chronic Conditions must total two or more for a patient to be billable under CPT 99490). - Related workflow: enrollment wizard Step 2 (chronic conditions) → ongoing Follow Up / care coordination logs Service Time. - Where it appears: CCM lookup report (Eligible CPT Codes column), Billing Management CCM report, Patients tab CPT Billing card (CCM view, e.g., 99490/99491/99439 counters).
CPT 99439 — CCM Care Coordination, Each Additional 20 Minutes (Clinical Staff) - Description per the manual: additional-time companion code to 99490. - Required conditions: same chronic-condition requirement as 99490, plus additional accrued Service Time beyond the first 20 minutes. - Where it appears: same reports as 99490.
CPT 99491 — CCM Care Coordination, Physician-Provided - Description per the manual: reflects physician-provided CCM time rather than clinical-staff time; eligibility is “based on Service Time and provider type.” - Where it appears: CCM lookup report and Billing Management CCM report, alongside 99490/99439.

task: 14.3. CPT Code Reference (complete set documented in the source manual)
text:
“Eligible CPT Codes” on every report is a live, system-calculated column — it is never manually entered — listing every code the patient currently qualifies for in the selected billing window based on recorded Measurement Days, Service Time, Chronic Conditions count, and (for CCM) Complexity/Billing Path.
A dash (“–”) in the Eligible CPT Codes column means the patient is not yet eligible for any code in that window.
Export and Email on any billing/lookup report use whichever filters are currently applied — narrow the results first if the report is being generated for someone outside the current view.
Status colors on billing screens follow the convention used elsewhere on the Practice List: green = Active, red = Locked / needs attention (the exact universal color legend beyond this general statement is not specified in the user guide).

Navigation. Sidebar → Billing → eye icon (View Report) on a practice row → RPM tab (selected by default).
Preconditions. The practice has at least one patient enrolled in RPM for the selected billing period.
Outcome. A “Billing & Reports → [Practice Name]” page opens, header shows “RPM Billing Period: mm/dd/yyyy ~ mm/dd/yyyy,” with a filter panel above a per-patient results grid.
Filters: CPT Code, Patient Name, Insurance, minimum Service Time, RPM Service Date Range (mm/dd/yyyy ~ mm/dd/yyyy), Model #, Serial #, Measurement Days, Status, Caregiver, Provider, “Select Data for the Report” (choose which fields are included in an export).
Actions: Query (load results), Reset (clear all filters), Print (printable view), Export (dropdown, download the report), Email (send it).
Results grid columns: #, Status, Vitals, Patient Name, DOB, Model #, Serial #, RPM Start Date, Upload Date/Time, Measurement Days, Service Time, Caregiver, Provider, Eligible CPT Codes.
Procedure: 1. The RPM tab is selected by default when the practice’s billing report opens. 2. Filter by CPT Code, Patient Name, and/or Insurance to narrow results. 3. Filter by minimum Service Time and/or an RPM Service Date Range. 4. Filter by Model #, Serial #, Measurement Days, and/or Status. 5. Pick a Caregiver and/or Provider, and use “Select Data for the Report” for exports. 6. Click Query to load, Reset to clear, Print/Export/Email to distribute. 7. Review each row’s columns; use the Search box (top-right of the grid) or column-header sort to work the results.

Navigation. Same “Billing & Reports → [Practice Name]” page → click CCM next to RPM to switch tabs; header updates to “CCM Billing Period: mm/dd/yyyy ~ mm/dd/yyyy.”
Filters: CPT Code, Patient Name, Insurance (same as RPM tab), Service Time, CCM Service Date Range, Status, Caregiver, Provider, “Select Data for the Report.”
Results grid columns: #, Status, Patient Name, DOB, Clinical Min (clinical-staff minutes), Provider Min (physician minutes), Complexity (Non-Complex / Complex), Billing Path, Caregiver, Provider, Eligible CPT Codes.
Procedure: 1. Click CCM next to RPM to switch tabs. 2. Filter by CPT Code, Patient Name, Insurance (same as RPM tab). 3. Filter by Service Time, CCM Service Date Range, and/or Status. 4. Pick Caregiver and/or Provider; use Select Data for the Report for exports. 5. Use the same Reset/Query/Print/Export/Email controls as the RPM tab. 6. Review each row; use the Show-entries dropdown and pager (bottom-right) to page through a long CCM roster.
Business rules / notes. Complexity and Billing Path reflect the patient’s care-plan configuration for the cycle — they are not manually entered on this screen.

task: 14.6. Programs Module — Where CPT Codes Are Attached to a Care Program
text:
What it is / why it exists. The Programs module (Super Admin only; Sidebar → Programs) defines the care programs practices can enroll patients into. Each program bundles a category, billing codes, reimbursement values, clinical requirements, and a visual identity (badge color, icon).
Add Care Program — three sections of the wizard/form:
Section 1 — Program Identity:
Field | Description
Short Name | Compact label used on badges (e.g., CCM, RPM).
Category | Program family, chosen from a dropdown.
Full Name | Long-form name shown to clinicians.
Description | Purpose and scope.
Badge Color | Color chip used on cards and badges.
Section 2 — Billing & Coding:
Field | Description
Program Icons | Iconography used across dashboards.
CPT Codes | Comma-separated codes (e.g., “99457, 99458”).
Reimbursement Type | Fixed / Per-minute / Tiered.
Avg. Monthly Reimbursement ($) | Planning input for revenue estimates.
Section 3 — Clinical Requirements:
Field | Description
ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes | Search-and-select qualifying diagnoses, filtered by category.
Min. Enrollment Period (Days) | Minimum number of days a patient must remain enrolled.
Patient Consent Required | Consent policy for enrolling patients into the program.
Procedure: 1. Sidebar → Programs → + Add Program. 2. Enter Short Name, choose Category, enter Full Name and Description, pick a Badge Color. 3. Scroll to Billing & Coding: choose the Program Icon, enter comma-separated CPT Codes, choose Reimbursement Type, enter the Avg. Monthly Reimbursement. 4. Scroll to Clinical Requirements: select qualifying ICD-10 diagnoses, set the Minimum Enrollment Period, set the Patient Consent Required policy. 5. Click Save Program; the program appears in the catalogue.
Programs List — what’s on screen. Summary cards: Total Programs (number configured), Billing Codes (total CPT codes across all programs), Categories (distinct program categories); a + Add Program button.
Privileges. View: Yes. Add: Yes (+ Add Program runs the three-section wizard). Edit: Yes (edit any section, save). Delete: Yes (delete a care program that is not in use).
Cross-module relationship. The CPT codes attached to a program here (e.g., “99457, 99458” for RPM) are the same codes that later appear as “Eligible CPT Codes” on patient-level reports once a patient enrolled in that program meets the Measurement-Days/Service-Time/Chronic-Conditions thresholds documented in Section 14.3.

What it is / why it exists. Calendar defines what a visit is (Visit Type), when caregivers/providers are working (Working Hours), and provides the visual schedule grid used to book patients.
Who uses it. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider — all with View/Add/Edit/Delete = Yes. Practice Caregiver and System Caregiver have no Calendar module in their sidebar at all.
Navigation. Sidebar → Calendar, exposing three sub-items: Visit Type, Working Hours, Calendar (the grid). The recommended order of configuration is: configure visit types first, then working hours, then book on the grid.

Purpose. Define the appointment types (name, description, duration, color) available when booking on the calendar.
What’s on screen. Visit Type List: #, Practice Name, Visit Type, Visit Type Description, Duration, Status, Color, Action. Empty state: “No visit types found.”
Procedure: 1. Sidebar → Calendar → Visit Type. 2. Use the Search box to check whether a similar visit type already exists. 3. Click + Add Visit Type (top-right). 4. Enter Practice Name (for roles that see multiple practices), Visit Type name, Visit Type Description, Duration (minutes), Status (Active/Inactive), and pick a Color swatch. 5. Click Save. 6. Use row Action icons (pencil/trash) to edit or delete an existing type.
Business rules / notes: Duration drives the default appointment length on the calendar grid — e.g., a 30-minute visit type spans two 15-minute slots. Color is the block color shown on the calendar in day/week views; pick contrasting shades for adjacent visit types. Inactive visit types are hidden from the booking dropdown but remain shown on past appointments.

Purpose. Set the practice’s (or, for a Provider, their own) bookable office hours for each day of the week within a date range.
What’s on screen. Office Hours panel: Start Date (required), optional End Date, a checkbox per day of week (Sun–Sat), Start Time/End Time per active day (default 09:00 AM – 05:00 PM), a green + in the Action column to add an extra time block for split shifts.
Procedure: 1. Sidebar → Calendar → Working Hours. 2. Set the Start Date (required) and optional End Date for the schedule window. 3. Tick the checkbox next to each day the practice/provider is open. 4. For each active day, adjust Start Time and End Time. 5. Click the green + to add an additional time block on that day (e.g., a morning and an afternoon block). 6. Click Save to publish the schedule.
Business rules / notes: Days left unchecked are treated as closed — no appointments can be booked on those days. Leaving End Date blank keeps the schedule active indefinitely until edited. Overlapping time blocks on the same day are prevented by validation. If “No working hours available for this day” appears on the Calendar grid, revisit Working Hours to enable the day or extend the date range.

Purpose. Browse the appointment grid, pick a slot granularity, view assignments by caregiver/provider, and book, reschedule, or cancel appointments.
What’s on screen. A month mini-calendar, a slot-granularity dropdown (default 15 Minutes), a Week/List view toggle, a System Caregivers checklist (to overlay specific caregivers’ bookings), and the main grid itself, color-coded by Visit Type.
Procedure: 1. Sidebar → Calendar → Calendar. 2. Use the previous/next month arrows to move between months. 3. Click any date to load that day’s slot list in the right-hand panel. 4. Change slot granularity via the dropdown. 5. Click the refresh icon to reload appointments after external changes. 6. Toggle Week/List (top-right) to switch layouts. 7. In the System Caregivers panel, tick one or more caregivers to overlay their bookings on the grid. 8. Click Clear to remove a date filter, or Today to jump to the current date. 9. Click an empty slot to open the Add Appointment / booking dialog — pick Patient, Visit Type, System Caregiver/Provider, Start, End, and Notes, then Save. 10. Click an existing appointment to view detail; drag to reschedule, or click Edit to change time/attendees. 11. Click Cancel Appointment to remove it and notify the patient.
Business rules / notes: Only slots inside the configured Working Hours are clickable — greyed-out slots are outside availability. Rescheduling triggers an automatic patient notification per the practice’s SMS/email preferences. Ticking a caregiver adds their name to the visible legend so overlapping appointments can be distinguished by color.

What it is / why it exists. Messages is the platform’s built-in, HIPAA-secured chat, letting operator roles communicate with caregivers, providers, and patients while reviewing a patient’s latest vitals alongside the conversation via the Focused Vital Snapshot panel. Messages are stored inside the practice tenant, not sent as email.
Who uses it. Every operator role (Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, System Caregiver) has View=Yes, Add=Yes (start a new conversation), Edit=Not applicable (sent messages cannot be edited), Delete=No (conversations are not deleted, only archived/muted from this screen).
Navigation. Sidebar → Messages.
What’s on screen. Three-pane layout: Conversations (left), Thread pane (center), Focused Vital Snapshot (right). All/Unread (and, for some roles, Flagged) tabs above the conversation list; a Search conversations box; a kebab (⋮) menu for bulk actions (mark all read, mute, archive / “Select chats”); a + floating action button (bottom-left) to start a new conversation.
Procedure: 1. Open Messages; the three-pane layout loads. 2. Use Search conversations, or the All/Unread(/Flagged) tabs, to find a thread. 3. Click a conversation to load it in the center pane; empty state: “Your Messages — Select a contact from the list or start a new conversation to collaborate.” 4. Click the + button to start a new conversation — pick recipient(s), optionally attach a patient, and type the message. 5. Use the three-dot menu for bulk actions. 6. In the Focused Vital Snapshot pane, search a patient by name or ID to preview their latest BP/Glucose/Weight readings alongside the conversation. 7. Use flag/unread controls inside a message to change its state; flagged messages appear under the Flagged tab (where available).
Business rules / notes. Attaching a patient to a conversation logs the reference to that patient’s audit trail. Unread counts on the Messages sidebar badge reflect only the current user’s inbox.

The Settings module contains several sub-tabs whose exact set varies by role. The maximal set (Super Admin) is: Account, Follow Up, Permission, Email Logs, Mobile App, Calendar Permission, Chat Access. Practice Admin/Provider/Practice Caregiver/System Caregiver see a subset: Account, Follow Up, Calendar Permission, Chat Access (Permission, Email Logs, and Mobile App are Super-Admin/Admin-only, platform-level surfaces).

Purpose. Every role’s own login profile and session controls.
Navigation. Sidebar → Settings → Account (default sub-tab).
What’s on screen / fields. Full Name, Username (read-only), Email (read-only), Phone, Fax, Two Way Authentication status chip (Enabled/green or Disabled/red), Session Time (minutes, editable), Clear Cache/Refresh control.
Procedure: 1. Open Settings; the Account tab is selected by default. 2. Review Full Name, Username, Email, Phone, Fax. 3. Check the Two Way Authentication chip. 4. Enter a new value under Session Time (minutes) and click Update/Save to change how long an idle session stays signed in. 5. Click Refresh next to Clear Cache to clear locally cached data for the current browser session.
Business rules / notes: Username, Email, and the assigned role are always read-only on this tab — provisioned when the account is created; changed only by a Practice Admin/System Admin/Super Admin elsewhere. Session Time applies to future sign-ins — it does not shorten or extend the currently active session. For Super Admin specifically, this tab additionally supports full password change (current password + new password twice, validated live) and a 2FA toggle in the same panel — this is documented in the Super Admin chapter but not repeated verbatim for every other role’s Account tab, where Session Time and Clear Cache are the primary editable controls documented.

Purpose. A library of reusable note templates for patient follow-up calls, capturing structured clinical observations, recommended actions, and (for CCM) care-management contact records, so caregivers don’t retype boilerplate for every patient.
Who can manage templates. Every operator role (Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, System Caregiver) can View/Add/Edit/Delete Follow Up templates.
Navigation. Sidebar → Settings → Follow Up.
What’s on screen. Table: #, Template Name, Content (preview), Action (Edit/Delete). A Search box and an Add Template button (top-right).
Procedure: 1. Open Settings → Follow Up. 2. Review the template list. 3. Use the Search box to filter by template name. 4. Click Add Template (top-right). 5. Enter a Template Name (e.g., “Normal BP,” “CCM – Care Plan Review”). 6. Write the Content — templates may include structured parameter fields (Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate), symptom/adherence statement lines, checkbox-style recommended actions, a CCM “care management contact completed” line, and Conditions Addressed / Activity fields. 7. Click Save; the template becomes available for selection during care-management follow-up sessions. 8. Use the pencil icon to edit, or the trash icon to delete (with confirmation).
Business rules / notes: Templates created here are shared at practice level (or platform-wide for Super Admin/Admin) and available to all caregivers performing follow-ups. Deleting a template does not affect follow-up records already submitted using it. Example built-in templates: “Normal BP” (vitals + adherence) and “CCM – Care Plan Review” (care plan goals, barriers, patient education). Best practice noted in the Provider chapter: keep the parameter lines (Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate, Date/Time) blank in the template so the caregiver fills them from the actual reading; keep separate RPM (vitals review) and CCM (care-plan review) templates because the two programs bill different CPT codes.

task: 17.3. Permission (Role-Based Access Control) — Super Admin / Admin
text:
Purpose. The RBAC surface. Every eVitals user is assigned exactly one role; the role determines which menus, screens, and operations that user can access. This tab lets a Super Admin create custom roles, edit existing roles, and assign users to roles.
Navigation. Sidebar → Settings → Permission.
What’s on screen. Role List table: Role Id, Role Name, Action (Edit / Assign User). Pagination: Show [N] entries, Page [1] of 1. Built-in roles listed: Super Admin (1), Admin (2), Practice Admin (3), Provider (4), Practice CareGiver (5), Patient (6), System Caregiver (7), superadminrole (9).
Procedure — review roles: 1. Open Settings → Permission. 2. Review the Role List. 3. Use Show [10] entries to adjust page size; use Search to filter by role name.
Procedure — create a custom role: 1. Click Add Role (top-right, next to Search). 2. Enter a descriptive role name; the Role Id is generated automatically. 3. Tick the modules and operations (View/Add/Edit/Delete) the role may perform — the permission matrix. 4. Click Save; the role appears in the Role List and can be assigned to users immediately.
Procedure — edit a role or assign users: 1. Click the Edit (pencil) icon on the role row; update the role name or permission matrix, then save. 2. Click the Assign User (person+) icon on the role row to link user accounts to that role.
Business rules / notes: Built-in roles cannot be deleted — only custom roles can be removed. Custom roles can be added without affecting the built-in role set. The Super Admin role (Role 1) has an Edit icon only — it cannot have users assigned through this interface. Every built-in role’s actual documented capabilities are described role-by-role in Section 3 of this document.

Purpose. Controls which System Caregivers can access a shared/practice/provider calendar and defines the exact operations (Create, View, Edit, Delete) each caregiver is permitted to perform.
Who can manage it. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, and Provider (for the Provider’s own calendar).
Navigation. Sidebar → Settings → Calendar Permission.
What’s on screen. A System Caregiver search/picker, four permission checkboxes (Create/View/Edit/Delete), a Save button, and a table of existing grants: #, System Caregiver, Permissions (colored pills), Created By, Actions (Edit/Delete). Empty state: “No permissions found.”
Procedure — grant access: 1. Open Settings → Calendar Permission. 2. Click the System Caregiver search/dropdown (mandatory field) and pick the target caregiver. 3. Tick one or more permissions: Create (add new calendar events), View (see calendar events), Edit (modify existing events), Delete (remove events). 4. Click Save (top-right). The caregiver row is added with the assigned permissions shown as colored pills.
Procedure — edit or remove access: 1. Locate the row (scroll or Search). 2. Click the Edit (pencil) icon to adjust the permission checkboxes and Save. 3. Click the Delete (trash) icon to remove the row — this revokes all calendar access for that caregiver.
Business rules / notes: Only System Caregivers appear in this search — Practice Caregivers are managed at the practice level, not here. The Created By column shows the admin account that last created/modified the row. A caregiver with no row in this table has no calendar access by default. Calendar Permission must be granted here before a System Caregiver can be assigned to book appointments on the Calendar grid. Revoking access does not delete appointments the caregiver already booked — those remain on the calendar. Permissions granted via a Provider’s own Calendar Permission tab apply only to that Provider’s own calendar, not to another provider’s.

Purpose. Controls which staff members are allowed to chat with which patients or with each other, on a per-practice basis, across three relationship types.
Who can manage it. Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin (documented; not documented as available to Provider, Practice Caregiver, or System Caregiver).
Navigation. Sidebar → Settings → Chat Access.
What’s on screen. A Practice dropdown (scopes the whole tab to one practice), three relationship-type tabs — Caregiver ↔ Patient, Provider ↔ Patient, Caregiver ↔ Provider — a left-hand list of staff (Caregivers or Providers) with a reachability badge (e.g., “0/259”), a right-hand list of the counterpart contacts with per-row Allowed/Blocked toggles, a “Can message X of Y” live summary line, Allow all / Block all buttons, a Search box, and All/Allowed/Blocked filter tabs.
Procedure: 1. Open Settings → Chat Access. 2. Choose the Practice from the dropdown. 3. Pick the relationship type: Caregiver ↔ Patient, Provider ↔ Patient, or Caregiver ↔ Provider. 4. Click a name in the left-hand list to load their access panel. 5. Use the search box, or the All/Allowed/Blocked filters, to review the linked patients or colleagues. 6. Flip an individual toggle to switch one person between Allowed and Blocked, or click Allow all / Block all to set every entry at once.
Business rules / notes: Caregiver↔Patient and Provider↔Patient both scope against the full patient list; Caregiver↔Provider scopes against the practice’s provider roster only. Counts (e.g., “0/259”) reflect how many of the possible contacts are currently allowed, not blocked. Chat Access changes take effect immediately in the Messages module — a Blocked pair cannot open a new conversation thread.

Purpose. The platform-wide audit trail of every outbound system email — OTPs, password resets, support tickets, system alerts.
Navigation. Sidebar → Email Logs (also reachable as Settings → Email Logs for Admin per the narrative Account Settings chapter, though it is not separately listed in Admin’s role-privileges-at-a-glance table — see Section 24).
What’s on screen / columns: #, Date, From (“E-Vitals” info@evitalsrpm.com), To, CC/BCC (N/A when none), Subject, Body (preview), Event (category, e.g., Send Otp, Change Password, N/A for transactional), Status (green S = sent successfully).
Procedure: 1. Sidebar → Email Logs. 2. Enter part of the subject, recipient, or event category in Search. 3. Read the Status pill. 4. Scroll the Body cell for the full message preview.
Privileges. View: Yes. Add: No (entries are system-written). Edit: No (immutable). Delete: No. Search/filter: Yes (by recipient, status, and date range).

Purpose. Controls which users of a selected practice are entitled to sign in to the eVitals mobile companion app. Access is scoped per practice and granted/revoked individually per user, and is independent of web-portal access — a user may hold one without the other.
Navigation. Sidebar → Settings → Mobile App (also has a standalone platform module reference in the Super Admin sidebar listing, section 12.13).
What’s on screen. A Practice dropdown (top-right); four summary cards — Total Users (all accounts linked to the selected practice), Mobile Enabled (accounts with active mobile access), Patients (patient accounts in the selected practice), Staff (caregiver and provider accounts). Below the cards, a user list with an on/off toggle per row.
Procedure: 1. Open Settings → Mobile App. 2. Select a Practice from the dropdown — the user list loads below the summary cards. Empty state before selection: “Select a Practice — Choose a practice from the dropdown above to manage which users can access the mobile app.” 3. Review the access summary cards. 4. Flip the toggle for the target user — Toggle ON grants mobile access; Toggle OFF revokes it immediately.
Business rules / notes: A practice must be selected before the user list appears. Summary card counts refresh automatically after toggling access.
This section consolidates every reporting/export surface documented in the source manual so a single retrieval can answer “what reports exist and what do they contain.”

Access: Patient Mgmt → Lookup Patient (all roles except System Caregiver’s Add-New-Patient variant; System Caregiver has this as a read-only lookup too).
Purpose: Find a patient by name/practice/provider/caregiver/status; shows latest vitals, not a date-scoped billing view.
Columns: Status, Vitals chips, Name, Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse, Glucose, Weight, Last Upload, # Readings, Time.
Export: Not explicitly documented with Print/Export/Email controls (contrast with the RPM/CCM date lookups below, which do document those controls).
Full detail: Section 9.3.

Access: Patient Mgmt → Lookup Patient (by RPM date).
Purpose: RPM service activity and CPT eligibility over a chosen date range.
Columns: Status, Vitals, Patient Name, DOB, Model #, Serial #, RPM Start Date, Upload Date/Time, Measurement Days, Service Time, Caregiver, Provider, Eligible CPT Codes.
Export: Print, Export (CSV/Excel), Email.
Full detail: Section 9.4.

Access: Patient Mgmt → Lookup Patient (by CCM date).
Purpose: CCM service activity, chronic conditions, and billing status over a chosen date range.
Columns: Status, Patient Name, DOB, Chronic Conditions, Enrollment Date, Last Activity, Service Time, Eligible CPT Codes, Billing.
Export: Print, Export, Email.
Full detail: Section 9.5.

task: 18.4. Billing Management — Practice List for Billing Report
text:
Access: Super Admin/Admin, Sidebar → Billing.
Purpose: Platform-/scope-wide roll-up of which practices are ready to bill.
Columns: ID, Status, Name, Phone 1, Email, Program Enrolled, Billing Period Date, Patients Status (T/A/P/L chips), View Report.
Full detail: Section 14.2.

Access: Billing → eye icon on a practice row → RPM tab.
Columns: #, Status, Vitals, Patient Name, DOB, Model #, Serial #, RPM Start Date, Upload Date/Time, Measurement Days, Service Time, Caregiver, Provider, Eligible CPT Codes.
Filters: CPT Code, Patient Name, Insurance, min. Service Time, RPM Service Date Range, Model #, Serial #, Measurement Days, Status, Caregiver, Provider, Select Data for the Report.
Export: Print, Export, Email.
Full detail: Section 14.4.

Access: Same page → CCM tab.
Columns: #, Status, Patient Name, DOB, Clinical Min, Provider Min, Complexity, Billing Path, Caregiver, Provider, Eligible CPT Codes.
Filters: CPT Code, Patient Name, Insurance, Service Time, CCM Service Date Range, Status, Caregiver, Provider, Select Data for the Report.
Export: Print, Export, Email.
Full detail: Section 14.5.

Access: Care Mgmt → Follow Up, all six operator roles.
Purpose: Work-list of patients needing outreach (missed uploads, abnormal readings, pending care-plan items).
Columns: Status, Vitals chips, Name, Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse, Glucose, Weight, Last Upload, # Readings, Time, Action.
Export: Print, Export, Email (documented for Practice Admin/Provider/System Caregiver variants).
Full detail: Section 13.4.

Access: Super Admin/Admin, Sidebar → Email Logs (or Settings → Email Logs).
Purpose: Platform-wide outbound-email audit trail.
Columns: #, Date, From, To, CC/BCC, Subject, Body, Event, Status.
Full detail: Section 17.6.

Access: A button/link at the bottom of most role/practice-user grids — Admins, Providers, Caregivers, System Caregivers, Inventory, Billing, Schedule & Targets sub-tabs, Follow Up templates, Calendar Permission, Admins tab, etc.
Purpose: Chronological history of add/edit/delete/assignment/status-change actions for that specific grid.
Note: Event Logs is a per-screen audit control, distinct from the platform-wide Email Logs module. The exact column layout of an opened Event Logs view is not specified in the user guide beyond “a chronological list of admin actions (add, edit, status change, login)” given as an example for the Admins tab.

Access: Inventory list → eye icon on a product.
Purpose: Trace every physical serial number mapped to a product and its assignment status.

This section connects the module-by-module detail above into the end-to-end chains a RAG system needs to answer “how are X and Y related” questions.

task: 19.1. Practice Provisioning → Staffing → Patient Enrollment Chain
text:
Super Admin provisions a new Practice via Enrollment (Section 7), setting Practice Detail, the first Admin Detail, Practice Settings (password criteria, 2FA, email notifications), and the RPM/CCM Care Program Billing Cycles (Start Date + cycle length in Days → auto-computed End Date).
Within that practice, Practice Admins, Providers, and Practice Caregivers are added via the practice detail’s Admins/Providers/Caregivers tabs (Section 6.4–6.6) — by Super Admin, Admin, or Practice Admin, depending on role.
Optionally, a System Caregiver from the platform-wide pool (Section 8.2) is assigned to the practice by Super Admin/Admin; this makes them visible (read-only) on the practice’s System Caregivers tab (Section 6.8) but does not by itself grant calendar or chat access — those are separate grants (Sections 17.4, 17.5).
A Patient is enrolled (Section 9.2) by a Practice Admin, Provider, or Practice Caregiver, requiring an assigned Provider and at least one Practice Caregiver as part of Demographics (Step 1).
On Programs (Step 2), the patient is enrolled into CCM (needs ≥2 Chronic Conditions) and/or RPM (needs ≥1 monitored vital).
If RPM, Step 3 binds a device — drawn from the practice’s/platform’s Inventory pool (Section 12) — via Model Number + 16-character Serial Number, and sets the RPM Start Date, which becomes the anchor for the practice’s RPM billing cycle for that patient.

Device assignment → vital transmission → reading classification → measurement/service-time accrual → CPT eligibility → billing report, is documented in full in Section 12.8. In one line: Patient enrollment binds a Serial Number to a patient → the device uploads readings → Schedule & Targets classifies each reading as in-range/abnormal → qualifying upload-days accumulate as Measurement Days and caregiver review time accumulates as Service Time → these numbers are evaluated against the CPT rules in Section 14.3 → the result is shown as “Eligible CPT Codes” on the RPM/CCM Lookup reports (Sections 9.4–9.5) and the Billing Management RPM/CCM reports (Sections 14.4–14.5).

task: 19.3. Abnormal Reading → Follow Up → Documentation Chain
text:
A reading arrives outside the practice’s configured Schedule & Targets range (Section 11) and is flagged abnormal (rendered in red/amber) on the Patients grid.
The patient becomes eligible to surface in a Follow Up Query (Section 13.4) run from Care Mgmt, alongside patients with missed uploads or pending care-plan items.
A caregiver/provider acts on the flagged row, optionally using a Follow Up Template (Section 17.2) to pre-fill structured documentation (vitals, symptom/adherence checklist, recommended actions, CCM contact-completed line).
The time spent on this follow-up contributes to the patient’s Service Time, which feeds back into CPT eligibility (Section 14.3) for both RPM (99457/99458) and CCM (99490/99439/99491).
Dismissing the follow-up row from the queue does not delete the underlying missed-upload/abnormal-reading event itself.

A Practice Admin, Provider, Super Admin, or Admin grants a named System Caregiver Create/View/Edit/Delete rights via Settings → Calendar Permission (Section 17.4).
Only after that grant exists can the System Caregiver appear in the “System Caregivers” overlay checklist on the Calendar grid (Section 15.4) and be assigned to bookings.
Bookings on the grid draw their appointment-type list from Visit Type (Section 15.2) and are constrained to the Working Hours (Section 15.3) configured for that practice/provider.
A System Caregiver with no Calendar Permission row has no visibility into the calendar at all, even though they may be actively assigned to the practice via the System Caregivers roster (Section 6.8/8.2/10).

Super Admin, Admin, or Practice Admin configures Chat Access (Section 17.5) per practice and per relationship type (Caregiver↔Patient, Provider↔Patient, Caregiver↔Provider), defaulting individual pairs to Allowed or Blocked.
Only Allowed pairs can open or continue a conversation thread in Messages (Section 16); a newly Blocked pair cannot start a new thread. This takes effect immediately.
Inside Messages, the Focused Vital Snapshot panel pulls the same underlying vitals data documented in the Vitals/RPM sections (Section 13.1) into the chat context when a patient is searched.

Super Admin defines a Care Program (Section 14.6) — Short Name/Category/Full Name, attached CPT Codes (comma-separated), Reimbursement Type, and Clinical Requirements (qualifying ICD-10 diagnoses, minimum enrollment period, consent policy).
A practice’s patients are enrolled into that program’s Short Name (CCM/RPM) during the enrollment wizard’s Programs step (Section 9.2.2).
The same CPT codes configured on the Program record are what later appear, patient-by-patient, as “Eligible CPT Codes” once Measurement-Days/Service-Time/Chronic-Conditions thresholds (Section 14.3) are met.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text: This section compiles every documented validation rule, blocking condition, warning, and empty-state message from across the source manual, organized by the module in which it occurs.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
Condition | System behavior
No Practice Caregiver selected on Step 1 | Next is blocked with the message “Select at least one practice caregiver” — required even for RPM-only enrollments.
Required demographic fields incomplete (First Name, Last Name, Gender, DOB, SSN, Home Phone, Cell Phone) | Next stays disabled until all are valid.
Neither CCM nor RPM toggled on Step 2 | At least one program must be enabled to proceed.
Meter Serial Number not exactly 16 characters | Save Patient / Next is disabled until the length matches.
Serial Number already bound to another patient | Rejected — the meter must be unassigned from the other patient first.
Fewer than two Chronic Conditions selected for a CCM patient | Patient is not billable under CPT 99490 (a data/billing-eligibility issue rather than a hard form block, per the CCM lookup report Notes).

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
A row with a duplicate MRN is skipped, not created as a duplicate patient (idempotent-by-MRN behavior).
A row whose CCM/RPM start date falls outside the practice’s active billing cycle is rejected.
Provider and Caregiver selections apply to every row in the file; a practice needing different assignments per patient must split the file into multiple imports.
Failed rows are reported back with a row-level error list; a confirmation toast reports how many rows succeeded vs. failed.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
Deleting a product with any still-assigned mapped device is blocked — devices must be unassigned first, or the product set Inactive instead.
Decreasing a product’s Qty below its number of already-mapped serials is blocked by validation.
Assigned serials cannot be changed from the Edit Products modal — the modal displays “Assigned serials cannot be changed from this screen”; changes must go through Inventory Details → Mapped device.
Setting product Status = Inactive preserves history but blocks new assignments.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
Overlapping BP reading windows across the five bands are rejected by validation (“Windows must not overlap — validation flags any conflicts before Save is accepted”).
BG windows must be chronological — e.g., a Before-Lunch start earlier than the Lunch anchor set in Daily Schedule is rejected.
Weight Target Range and Body Fat Target Range validate that the lower bound is less than the upper bound.
The Evening weight window may span midnight (end time earlier than start time); the system treats this as an overnight interval rather than an error.
Weight-target changes take effect only on the next uploaded reading — historical readings are not retroactively reclassified.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
Overlapping Working Hours time blocks on the same day are prevented by validation.
Days left unchecked in Working Hours are treated as closed — no bookings possible.
Only slots inside configured Working Hours are clickable on the booking grid; other slots are greyed out.
“No working hours available for this day” is shown on the Calendar grid when the selected day has no configured hours.
“No visit types found” is the empty state shown until at least one Visit Type is saved.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
“No permissions found” is the empty state on Calendar Permission until a first System Caregiver grant is saved.
A System Caregiver with no Calendar Permission row has no calendar access by default, regardless of practice assignment.
Revoking a caregiver’s Calendar Permission does not delete appointments they already booked.
A Chat Access pair toggled to Blocked immediately cannot open a new conversation thread in Messages.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
Deleting the last Active Practice Admin on a practice is blocked, to prevent account lock-out.
Email addresses must be unique across the entire eVitals platform — reusing an existing address is blocked when adding a new user.
Setting a caregiver/provider Status = Inactive preserves the historical record but prevents sign-in and removes them from selectable lists on new assignments.
Email changes on a caregiver record trigger a verification email if two-factor authentication is enabled.
Deleting a caregiver is discouraged (in favor of Inactive) when the caregiver has historical patient interactions, because deletion is irreversible; the system additionally warns/blocks deletion of a caregiver with active patient assignments (System Admin chapter: “The caregiver has no active patient assignments (system will warn otherwise)”).
Session Time changes apply only to future sign-ins, not the currently active session.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
A practice with Status = Inactive blocks new device orders, uploads, and billing until reactivated.
A practice is deactivated, never deleted, from the UI (Super Admin’s Practice List Delete = “Deactivate only”).

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases
text:
“Select filters and click Query to load patients” is the empty state shown on every Lookup Patient screen until Query is run.
Query is the only trigger on Lookup Patient screens — changing a filter alone does not reload the grid.
On the Provider/Practice-Caregiver/System-Caregiver variants of Lookup Patient, Program Enrolled is a required filter and Query stays disabled until it is chosen.
A dash (“–”) in Model # or Serial # on an RPM report signals an incomplete device binding that must be fixed on the patient profile before billing.
A dash in the Eligible CPT Codes column means the patient is not yet eligible for any code in the selected window.

module: 20. Errors, Warnings, Validation Rules, and Edge Cases

Built-in roles cannot be deleted; only custom roles can be removed.
The Super Admin role (Role Id 1) exposes only an Edit action in the Permission table — it cannot be assigned to users through the Assign User control shown for other roles.

module: 22. Coverage and Known Discrepancies in the Source Manual
text:
This knowledge base was built from a full read of the source manual’s structural text (headings, task meta-boxes, numbered steps, UI Reference tables, and Notes callouts) across every documented role chapter. The following points are flagged explicitly, per the requirement to mark gaps rather than invent answers, and to surface internal inconsistencies found in the source itself rather than silently resolving them:
1. Super Admin’s Patient Management row conflict. The Super Admin “Role privileges at a glance” table (source Section 12) lists Patient Management as View=No / Add=No / Edit=No / Delete=No, while the narrative Patient Management section for Super Admin (source Section 12.7) describes the Super Admin running Lookup Patient / Lookup Patient by RPM date / Lookup Patient by CCM date with search, filter, and export. This document reports both as written (Section 3.1) rather than resolving the conflict, since the source manual itself does not reconcile it.
2. Admin’s Email Logs / Permission visibility. Admin’s “Role privileges at a glance” table (source Section 13) does not list Email Logs, Permission, or Mobile App Access as rows. However, the narrative Admin Account Settings chapter (source Section 13.9) documents Email Logs and Permission sub-tabs with full step-by-step procedures under the Admin actor. This document notes both facts (Section 3.2, Section 17.6) rather than assuming one supersedes the other.
3. Numeric password-strength criteria. Multiple screens reference “password criteria” (length, case, digit, symbol rules) as being “shown live under the password field,” but the source manual never states the actual numeric thresholds (e.g., minimum length). This is marked Not specified in the user guide wherever referenced.
4. Session Time default and maximum. The Account tab documents a configurable “Session Time (minutes)” field but does not state its default value or any maximum/minimum bound.
5. MRN field origin. The Import Patients idempotency rule references “MRN” as the deduplication key, but the enrollment wizard’s own field list (Section 9.2.1) does not explicitly name an “MRN” field among the Personal Information / Account Credentials fields — the manual does not clarify whether MRN is a distinct field, a synonym for a documented field (e.g., an internal record ID), or a bulk-import-only concept. Marked Not specified in the user guide.
6. CCM “Billing Path” enumerated values. The CCM billing report documents a “Billing Path” column and states it is derived from the care plan, but never enumerates the possible values it can take. Marked Not specified in the user guide (Section 13.3, 14.5).
7. Universal color-coding legend. Several screens reference color-coded status indicators (red = abnormal/Locked/needs-attention, green = Active/sent-successfully) but the manual does not provide one master legend covering every color used across every module — only per-context statements. This document has consolidated every explicit color statement it found (Sections 13.1, 14.2, 14.3) and flags that a comprehensive universal legend is not specified in the user guide.
8. Provider’s “Conditional” Edit right on Practice Caregivers. The Provider role-privileges table lists Edit = “Conditional” for Practice Caregivers with no further explanation of the condition. Reported verbatim in Section 3.4; the condition itself is not specified in the user guide.
9. Exact RPM billing-cycle default length. The documented example shows a 30-day RPM billing window (07-27-2026 – 08-26-2026), and Enrollment lets a Super Admin set an arbitrary “Days” value per practice — but the manual does not state a universal default cycle length that applies before a practice-specific value is configured.
10. This document does not cover the Patient (mobile app) role’s own screens. The source manual’s scope, as stated in its Overview, defines “Patient” as the end user of the mobile companion app, but the guide volume that was provided documents only the six operator/staff roles (Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, System Caregiver). No patient-facing mobile screens are described in the source, so none are described here.
Overall coverage statement. Every role chapter (Super Admin, Admin, Practice Admin, Provider, Practice Caregiver, System Caregiver), every sidebar module documented for at least one role, every numbered task/procedure, every UI Reference table, every CPT code, every device/serial-number rule, every Schedule & Targets default value, and every explicitly stated business rule/validation/warning encountered during a full read of the source manual has been captured in this knowledge base. This is not a claim of 100% completeness relative to the underlying eVitals product — it is a claim of completeness relative to the text of the provided source manual (Version 2.4), which is itself the authoritative source for this document per its own framing instructions.
End of eVitals RPM Platform Knowledge Base.
Module: 11. Schedule & Targets
Task: 11.7. Clinical Meaning of Colors
Subtask: Color Codes
Clinically, the color codes on vital readings indicate the following: Red indicates that a reading is in the danger zone, while Green indicates that a reading is healthy. This applies to all vital readings across the platform.
